items.title: Group schemes over a base scheme
items.statement: Let $S$ be a scheme. An $S$-group scheme is a group object in the category of $S$-schemes: an $S$-scheme $G$ together with $S$-morphisms $m:G\times_SG\to G$ (multiplication), $e:S\to G$ (unit section) and $i:G\to G$ (inverse) such that associativity, the two unit laws and the two inverse laws hold as identities of $S$-morphisms. A morphism of $S$-group schemes is an $S$-morphism compatible with $m,e,i$. Commutativity, closed subgroup schemes, normal subgroup schemes, kernels of morphisms, and the base change $G_{S'}=G\times_SS'$ with its induced $S'$-group structure are defined by the evident diagrams. This generalizes the field case of [[def-group-scheme-over-a-field]] and quotes no new existence statement.

Raynaud, Neron Models, Ergebnisse der Mathematik und ihrer Grenzgebiete (3) 21, Springer 1990 (Chapter 1 sections 1-2, Chapter 2 section 2.5, Chapter 3 sections 3.1-3.5, Chapter 4 sections 4.2-4.4, Chapter 7 section 7.2, Chapter 8 section 8.1, Chapter 10 section 10.2)

items.title: Finite etale schemes over a complete local ring and splitting
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $R$ be a Noetherian local ring which is complete and separated for its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, with residue field $k$, and let $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a finite etale $R$-scheme. Then the reduction map $Y(R)\to Y(k)$ is a bijection. If in addition $k$ has no nontrivial finite separable field extension, then every finite etale $R$-algebra of rank $d$ is isomorphic to $R^d$ as an $R$-algebra, and $Y$ is a disjoint union of $d$ copies of $\operatorname{Spec}R$.

items.title: S-dense open subschemes and S-rational maps
items.statement: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme and let $X$ and $Y$ be smooth $S$-schemes. An open subscheme $U\subseteq X$ is $S$-dense if for every $s\in S$ the fibre $U_s$ is Zariski dense in $X_s$; finite intersections of $S$-dense opens are $S$-dense, and the restriction of an $S$-dense open to an open subscheme is $S$-dense there. An $S$-rational map $u:X\dashrightarrow Y$ is an equivalence class of $S$-morphisms $U\to Y$ defined on $S$-dense open subschemes, where two are equivalent if they agree on an $S$-dense open subscheme of the intersection. The largest domain of definition is the union of the open domains on which representatives agree. For a separated smooth target and smooth finite-type schemes over a locally Noetherian base, its formation commutes with flat base change (BLR 2.5/6), with flatness an essential hypothesis. A collection of fibrewise rational maps with informal specialization compatibility is not used as an equivalent definition; an actual representative on an S-dense open is required.

references.title: S. Bosch, W. Lutkebohmert, M. Raynaud, Neron Models, Ergebnisse der Mathematik und ihrer Grenzgebiete (3) 21, Springer 1990 (2.5 S-Rational Maps, from the section opening through Proposition 6; Chapters 1-6, 7.2, 8.1)

items.title: A normal Noetherian domain is the intersection of its height-one localizations
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $A$ be a Noetherian normal domain with fraction field $K$. Then inside $K$ one has $A=\bigcap_{\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p=1}A_{\mathfrak p}$, the intersection running over the height-one prime ideals. Proof strategy: for z=b/a∉A with a≠0 the class of b in A/(a) is nonzero. Its cyclic submodule has an associated prime p (published existence and cyclic-embedding criteria), and b remains nonzero after localizing at p. The localized quotient has depth zero, while a is regular; the regular-element depth formula gives depth A_p=1. Normality implies S_2, so ht(p)≤1; since a∈p and a≠0, ht(p)=1. Thus z∉A_p. This proves the intersection formula by contraposition; the forward inclusion is immediate. Apply it to each function on an affine normal chart for the consequence that regularity at all height-one points implies global regularity.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Tag 031T and Tag 0AVK (Hartogs for normal domains)
Bosch, Lutkebohmert, Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 2.5/1 and scheme Hartogs in owner-arithmetic-models/neron-source/closure-supplement.md

items.title: Neron models and the Neron mapping property
items.statement: Let $S$ be a Dedekind scheme with function field $K$, and let $X_K$ be a smooth separated $K$-scheme of finite type. A Neron model of $X_K$ over $S$ is an $S$-model $X\to S$ which is smooth, separated and of finite type, and which satisfies the Neron mapping property: for every smooth $S$-scheme $Y$ and every $K$-morphism $u_K:Y_K\to X_K$ there is a unique $S$-morphism $u:Y\to X$ extending $u_K$. When $S$ is local, the local Neron model at the closed point is $X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{S,s}$. A weak Neron model is a smooth separated finite-type model satisfying the extension property for etale points, namely that every $K'$-point of $X_K$, where $R'$ is an etale DVR over a local DVR $R$ of $S$ and $K'=\operatorname{Frac}R'$, extends to $X$. The Neron mapping property for $Y=X$ shows that a Neron model is determined by its generic fibre up to a unique isomorphism; no existence is asserted by this definition.

items.title: The chord-tangent group law on a smooth short Weierstrass cubic
items.statement: Assume AC, inherited from RR and scheme-theoretic descent. Let k be a field of characteristic different from 2,3 and let 4a^3+27b^2≠0. The smooth projective cubic C:Y^2Z=X^3+aXZ^2+bZ^3 with O=[0:1:0] has the chord-tangent commutative group law, as an abelian variety over k. In affine coordinates, use λ=(y_2-y_1)/(x_2-x_1) or λ=(x_1^2+x_1x_2+x_2^2+a)/(y_1+y_2) where their denominators are nonzero; x(P+Q)=λ^2-x_1-x_2 and y(P+Q)=λ(x_1-x(P+Q))-y_1. At inverse pairs and doubled two-torsion points the sum is O. Complete strategy: the Jacobian computation gives smoothness after every field extension, and a reducible cubic would have intersecting geometric components by Bezout, contradicting smoothness; properness is projective. The published plane-curve genus formula gives genus one. RR and the trivial canonical bundle give the unique effective divisor of degree one in each degree-one line-bundle class over an algebraic closure; thus P↦[O(P-O)] bijects C(kbar) with Pic^0(C(kbar)) as the ordinary divisor-class group, without assuming a Picard scheme. A line section has divisor P+Q+R∼3O; for a vertical line P+(-P)+O∼3O. Therefore the chord-tangent operation transports divisor-class addition and satisfies all group identities. For algebraicity on (C\{O})^2 put (N,D)=(y_2-y_1,x_2-x_1) or (x_1^2+x_1x_2+x_2^2+a,y_1+y_2), and define projective coordinates [D(N^2-(x_1+x_2)D^2):N((2x_1+x_2)D^2-N^2)-y_1D^3:D^3]. These are regular on each open where (N,D) do not vanish simultaneously, including D=0,N≠0, where the value is O. The two opens cover the entire affine square: failure of the first means a diagonal pair, and failure of the second there would imply y=0 and 3x^2+a=0, contradicting smoothness. The curve equation and equality on overlap follow by substitution and the identity (y_2-y_1)(y_2+y_1)=(x_2-x_1)(x_2^2+x_1x_2+x_1^2+a). For each geometric R the fixed translation T_R is rational by these formulas and extends to C by the published smooth-curve/proper-target extension lemma; its inverse T_{-R} extends too, and the compositions are identity on a dense open, hence everywhere. For any (P,Q) choose R avoiding the two values -P and Q; then P+R and Q-R are finite, so m∘(T_R×T_{-R}) is regular on a neighbourhood of (P,Q). These neighbourhoods cover all geometric points; agreement on dense opens glues the maps over kbar. Uniqueness of the rational extension supplies the descent cocycle under kbar/k, and published fppf morphism descent gives m over k. The inverse [X:Y:Z]↦[X:-Y:Z] is regular. Group identities hold on geometric points and hence on the reduced products, yielding the abelian-variety structure.

references.title: J. S. Milne, Elliptic Curves, v2.0, Chapter III (Weierstrass equations and the group law)
D. Lombardo, Abelian varieties, Luxembourg Summer School on Galois representations lecture notes (2018), Chapter 1 sections 1-7

items.title: Affine commutative prime to characteristic torsion bound
items.statement:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the stated suppliers. over algebraically closed k, a smooth connected commutative affine group N of dimension a satisfies |N[ell^v](k)|≤ell^(va) for ell≠char k. Proof strategy: Statement: over algebraically closed k, a smooth connected commutative affine group N of dimension a satisfies |N[ell^v](k)|≤ell^(va) for ell≠char k.

Exact supplier: lem-nonaffine-affine-group-faithful-representation (arbitrary-field). Do NOT use lem-affine-algebraic-group-faithful-rational-representation, whose Statement is C-only. Split character algebra terminology may reuse lem-diagonalizable-character-antiequivalence.

Complete matrix proof: embed N in GL_m. The commuting point matrices generate a finite-dimensional commutative algebra of matrices. They have a common eigenvector: inductively take an eigenspace of one generator, stable under all others, and refine using a finite generating list until all act scalarly. Induct on the quotient dimension to obtain a common invariant flag. Matrix entries below the diagonal vanish at every k-point; reducedness and the Nullstellensatz make them zero as functions, so the group scheme embeds in upper triangular matrices. Let chi_i be its diagonal characters. The subalgebra of k[N] generated by chi_i and chi_i^-1 is a Hopf algebra k[M], with M=Z^m/L, L the relations among these characters. Distinct group-like elements are linearly independent: a shortest relation Σc_i h_i=0, coproduct minus its tensor product with h_1, gives Σ_(i>1)c_i h_i⊗(h_i-h_1)=0; independence of a proper sublist forces h_i=h_1, a contradiction. Thus no further linear relations occur. k[N] is a domain because N is smooth connected over algebraically closed k. Hence M is torsion-free: a nontrivial finite-order monomial yields nontrivial zero divisors or a nonzero nilpotent in k[M] from x^d-1. Therefore M≅Z^t, the diagonal image has torus coordinate ring k[M], and t≤a since its fraction field embeds in k(N). An element in the diagonal kernel is upper unitriangular. In characteristic zero, a unitriangular matrix of finite order d has minimal polynomial dividing both (X-1)^m and X^d-1; the latter is squarefree, so it is identity. In characteristic p, (I+U)^(p^e)=I for p^e≥m; an element also killed by ell^v must be identity by Bezout. Thus N[ell^v] injects into the diagonal torus's ell^v-torsion, of cardinal ell^(vt)≤ell^(va). No closed-image/splitting/unipotent-filtration result is needed.

references.title: Bosch, Lutkebohmert, Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 7.3/2-3 and 7.4/5; local proof route in owner-arithmetic-models/etale-source/closure-packet.md

items.title: Strict henselization of a DVR and smooth sections
items.statement:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied algebra and scheme results. For every DVR R, Rsh is a faithfully flat DVR with the same uniformizer and separably closed residue field; it is the filtered colimit of local etale R-algebras. Smooth schemes over a strictly henselian local ring lift rational special-fibre points to sections; those special points are dense. Complete proof strategy: Fix a separable closure ks of k. Use pointed local etale R-algebras with residue embeddings into ks; their fibre products and the chosen residue point make a directed system. Each such local algebra is flat over R; its maximal ideal is generated by pi, because its residue fibre is a separable field. Its local ring is regular of dimension one, hence a DVR. The transition maps are injective local maps and preserve pi. In the union Rsh, every nonzero element is pi to an integer power times a unit, as already true at a finite stage. Every nonzero ideal has a least such power, so is principal. Thus the union itself is a Noetherian DVR, without excellence. The union embeds in the chosen separable closure of K and is R-torsion-free, hence R-flat by the published PID criterion. Since the extension is local with the same nonzero residue fibre it is faithfully flat by the published criterion. Its residue field is ks. The etale-local universal property and henselian lifting follow directly: an etale neighbourhood and residue point involve finitely many coefficients and descend to a finite stage; adjoining that pointed neighbourhood to the directed system supplies its section in the limit. Consequently the union is strictly henselian.

For smooth V/Rsh and a special ks-point, choose differential coordinates at the point. Cutting out the coordinate differences gives an etale slice through it, with unchanged residue field (BLR 2.2/14, whose proof was read). The defining henselian property gives a section of that slice, and hence a section of V. Every nonempty smooth finite-type open over the separably closed field has a rational point by the exact published `lem-nonempty-smooth-scheme-finite-separable-point`; therefore these section specializations are dense. For the final generic-open-section clause, the base Lambda is a strictly henselian DVR, F is its fraction field, and the smooth integral model has nonempty special fibre. A dense open of its generic fibre also contains the generic point of a Lambda-section: the complement closure is horizontal and cannot contain a special-fibre component, so a special section outside that closure works. Equivalently one can use the relative dimension upper semicontinuity supplier below. This also proves the DVR specialization of BLR 5.3/7 needed in finite translate enlargement.

references.title: Bosch, Lutkebohmert, Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 2.2/13-14 and 2.3/5-10; local proof in owner-arithmetic-models/neron-source/closure-supplement.md

items.title: Finite Cartier duality, exactness and exponent
items.statement: Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied scheme and cohomology results. Finite commutative group schemes have a rank-preserving exact Cartier duality H↦H^D representing all-test Hom(H,G_m), with natural evaluation H≅H^{DD}; a rank-d finite commutative H is killed by d. Complete proof strategy: Let H be a finite commutative group scheme over a field k, B=O(H). The finite-dimensional vector-space dual B*=Hom_k(B,k), with multiplication dual to Delta_B and comultiplication dual to multiplication_B, is a commutative Hopf algebra. Its R-valued points are the group-like elements of B⊗R: the transpose of an algebra map B*→R is an element chi with Delta chi=chi⊗chi and counit1, exactly an all-test character H_R→G_m,R; its inverse is supplied by the antipode. Thus Spec B* represents H^D. Double vector-space duality is naturally Hopf-compatible, so H≅H^{DD}, with the evaluation pairing and rank equality. Finite commutative group schemes form an abelian category: the published normal-group quotient represents quotient by kernel; finite-type zero-dimensional separated schemes are finite (split into their finitely many local Artin charts), so quotient and image remain finite. The induced monomorphism from quotient to target is finite and hence closed; the target/image quotient supplies the cokernel. Their fppf sheaf kernel-image identities prove exactness. Cartier duality is an additive contravariant equivalence, therefore preserves exact sequences in reverse. To prove H killed by d=rankH, take an arbitrary character chi over R and h∈H(R). Translation conjugates multiplication by chi on the free rank-d algebra B⊗R, so Norm(t_h chi)=Norm(chi). But t_h chi=chi(h)chi; invertibility of Norm(chi) implies chi(h)^d=1. Apply this to the universal character on H^D and the bidual identification to get [d]H=0. This argument handles nonreduced schemes and characteristic dividing d. In particular mu_n^D is the constant group Z/n: the basis t^j of k[t]/(t^n-1) consists of group-like elements, so its dual algebra has the orthogonal idempotent basis of functions on Z/n, with coproduct given by addition modulo n.

references.title: Bosch, Lutkebohmert, Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 7.3/2-3 (finite Cartier duality and exponent)
B. Edixhoven, G. van der Geer, B. Moonen, Abelian Varieties (preliminary version 2012), Chapter 6 sections 1-3

items.title: Abelian schemes over a base
items.statement: Let $S$ be a scheme. An abelian scheme over $S$ of relative dimension $g$ is an $S$-group scheme $f:A\to S$ such that $f$ is smooth, proper and of finite presentation and every geometric fibre of $f$ is connected of dimension $g$. Equivalently, all fibres of $f$ are abelian varieties of dimension $g$ in the sense of [[def-abelian-variety-over-a-field]]; the relative dimension is locally constant on $S$ and equals $g$ on each connected component. The unit section $e:S\to A$ is a closed immersion and $A\to S$ is separated. No projectivity over $S$ is asserted; abelian schemes over a base need not be projective over that base.

references.title: B. Edixhoven, G. van der Geer, B. Moonen, Abelian Varieties (preliminary version 2012), Chapter 6 sections 1-3
D. Lombardo, Abelian varieties, Luxembourg Summer School on Galois representations lecture notes (2018), Chapter 1 sections 1-7 and Chapter 2 sections 4-5
S. Bosch, W. Lutkebohmert, M. Raynaud, Neron Models, Ergebnisse der Mathematik und ihrer Grenzgebiete (3) 21, Springer 1990, 1.2/8 and Chapter 7

items.title: An S-rational map defined after a faithfully flat smooth base change is defined
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $S$ be locally Noetherian, let $Y$ be separated over $S$ and let $u:X\dashrightarrow Y$ be an $S$-rational map between smooth finite-type $S$-schemes, and let $f:X'\to X$ be a faithfully flat morphism of smooth finite-type $S$-schemes such that the pullback $u\circ f:X'\dashrightarrow Y$ is represented by an $S$-morphism on all of $X'$. Then $u$ is represented by an $S$-morphism on all of $X$. The proof descends the representative of $u\circ f$ along the faithfully flat morphism $f$ using fppf descent of scheme morphisms; faithfulness of $f$ makes the descended morphism agree with every local representative of $u$ on an $S$-dense open. The descent cocycle is checked on X'×_X X': the two pullbacks agree on the pullback of the S-dense domain. Smooth fibres are geometrically reduced and fibrewise density makes that open schematically dense; separatedness then forces equality. Descent of morphisms supplies the extension and equality on the original domain. This is the proof of BLR 2.5/5; arbitrary base change is not used.

references.title: Bosch, Lutkebohmert, Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 2.5/5 (descent of S-rational maps)

items.title: Indeterminacy of a rational map into an affine scheme is of pure codimension one
items.statement: Assume AC. Let R be a ring, let Z be a normal Noetherian R-scheme and let B be a finitely generated R-algebra. For an R-rational map u:Z⇢Spec B the indeterminacy locus is empty or of pure codimension one. In particular if u is defined at every point of height at most one, it extends uniquely. Proof strategy: choose finitely many R-algebra generators b_i of B. On each integral affine chart of Z their images are rational functions. Their common regular locus is the domain of the map, since the finite equations of B vanish generically and therefore wherever all generators are regular. The pole locus of each rational function is a union of height-one closed subsets: if it is regular at all height-one points specializing to z, the local intersection formula for O_{Z,z} shows it regular at z, and it then extends to a neighbourhood. Finite intersections of the generator domains give the assertion. Finite generation over the base is needed to choose a common neighbourhood; this is sufficient for all affine neighbourhoods of the finite-type group scheme in the Weil extension theorem.

references.title: Bosch, Lutkebohmert, Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 4.4/2 (indeterminacy of maps into affine targets)
The Stacks Project, Tag 031T (Hartogs for normal schemes)

items.title: Uniqueness, weak Neron property, etale base change and local nature of Neron models
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $S$ be a Dedekind scheme with function field $K$ and let $X$ be a Neron model of the smooth separated finite-type $K$-scheme $X_K$. Then: (a) $X$ is unique up to a unique $S$-isomorphism; (b) $X$ is a weak Neron model: it satisfies the extension property for etale points, since the Neron mapping property applies to etale $Y$; (c) for every etale morphism $S'\to S$ with function field $K'$, the base change $X_{S'}$ is a Neron model of $X_{K'}$; (d) $X$ is a Neron model if and only if $X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{S,s}$ is a Neron model over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{S,s}$ for every closed point $s\in S$, and Neron models are local on the base; (e) if $X_K$ is a $K$-group scheme then the group law extends uniquely to $X$, making $X$ an $S$-group scheme. The arguments apply the mapping property directly, with limit arguments reducing morphisms of finite presentation over localizations to a neighbourhood of the point. No converse from the weak Neron property to the full mapping property is asserted for an arbitrary scheme or for a model whose generic fibre alone has a group law. For etale base change compose a smooth S'-source with S'→S, extend to X by the S-property, and combine that extension with its structure map to get the map to X_{S'}. For localization use finite presentation to spread the source and morphism over a neighbourhood, extend there, and glue by separatedness. Multiplication, inverse and identity extend by testing the property on X×_S X, X and S respectively; their identities hold by schematic density of the generic fibre, since the sources are smooth and hence flat over the Dedekind base.

references.title: S. Bosch, W. Lutkebohmert, M. Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 1.2/2-6 (uniqueness, weak property, etale base change, local nature, group law)

items.title: Two-torsion and uniqueness of the group law on a Weierstrass cubic
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field of characteristic not $2$ or $3$, let $a,b\in k$ with $4a^3+27b^2\neq0$, and let $C$ be the smooth cubic $Y^2Z=X^3+aXZ^2+bZ^3$ with $O=[0:1:0]$, regarded as an abelian variety by [[thm-plane-cubic-chord-tangent-group-law]]. Then: (a) the two-torsion subgroup of $C$ consists exactly of $O$ together with the three points $[x:0:1]$ with $x^3+ax+b=0$; in particular $C[2](k)=\{O\}$ if and only if the cubic $x^3+ax+b$ has no root in $k$; (b) if $C$ carries any abelian-variety structure with unit section $O$, then that group law equals the chord-tangent law, because the identity morphism from $(C,\cdot)$ to $(C,*)$ preserves the unit and is therefore a homomorphism by the pointed-morphism theorem, and its inverse gives the reverse implication. For (a), 2P=O iff P=-P. On the affine chart inversion is (x,y)↦(x,-y); in characteristic different from two this fixes precisely y=0, besides O. The cubic polynomial has three distinct geometric roots because its discriminant is nonzero. These are two-torsion points, not inflection points; inflections instead satisfy 3P=O. The pointed-homomorphism argument in (b) compares the two laws without assuming uniqueness in advance.

references.title: J. S. Milne, Elliptic Curves, v2.0, Chapter III (two-torsion and the group law)

items.title: Prime-to-residue-characteristic Tate modules and inertia
items.statement: Let A/K be an abelian variety, fix a separable closure K^sep, and let ell≠char K be prime. Define T_ell(A)=lim_{v≥1} A[ell^v](K^sep) with transition maps multiplication by ell, and Z_ell=lim Z/ell^v with the usual reduction transitions. Thus an element is a sequence a_v with ell a_{v+1}=a_v; coordinatewise scalar multiplication gives the Z_ell-module structure. Give this group the subspace topology from the product of the finite discrete torsion groups. Galois acts coordinatewise. For a DVR R with fraction field K and a chosen strict henselization R^sh embedded via its fraction field K^sh⊂K^sep, the inertia group is I=Gal(K^sep/K^sh). The Tate module is unramified at R if I acts trivially. This definition specifies the action and the test; no freeness or reduction criterion is assumed.

references.title: S. Bosch, W. Lutkebohmert, M. Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 7.4/5 and the Tate-module criterion for good reduction
J. S. Milne, Abelian Varieties, v2.00 (2008), Chapter I sections 3, 5, 8, 11, 17

items.title: Strict henselian etale sections
items.statement:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the stated suppliers. for a separated étale finite-type scheme H over a strictly henselian local ring R with separably closed residue field k, H(R)→H(k) is bijective. The finite part of H is a finite étale disjoint union of copies of Spec R containing its whole closed fibre; the complement has no R-sections. Proof strategy: Statement: for a separated étale finite-type scheme H over a strictly henselian local ring R with separably closed residue field k, H(R)→H(k) is bijective. The finite part of H is a finite étale disjoint union of copies of Spec R containing its whole closed fibre; the complement has no R-sections.

Exact earlier suppliers: thm-etale-locally-standard-etale; cor-henselian-local-simple-root-criterion; cor-idempotents-lift-uniquely-in-a-henselian-pair; thm-quasi-finite-algebra-open-finite-factorization for affine finite-part construction. Scheme finite-part construction may instead be bundled in this proof by gluing the section images below.

Complete local proof: for x∈H(k), choose its standard étale chart R[T]/(P) localized at g. The base neighbourhood contains the closed point of Spec R and therefore equals all of Spec R. The x-value a mod m is a simple root of the monic P; Hensel lifts it to a∈R, with g(a) a unit, giving a section. If two sections have equal reduction, their equalizer is open because an étale diagonal is open and closed because H is separated. It contains the closed point, hence is all of Spec R. A section image is open (base change of an étale diagonal) and closed (separatedness). Finitely many closed-fibre points give disjoint section images. Their finite disjoint union is the finite part, and its complement has empty closed fibre. Each R-section meets the closed fibre, so belongs to the finite part. This proves the finite-part assertion without a scheme-level Zariski Main Theorem prerequisite. Source: BLR7.3/3; expanded section argument supplies the omitted local details.

references.title: S. Bosch, W. Lutkebohmert, M. Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 7.3/3 (sections of etale schemes over strictly henselian rings)

items.title: The identity model of a smooth group with abelian generic fibre
items.statement:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied algebra and scheme results. Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$ and residue field $k$, and let $G$ be a smooth separated finite-type $R$-group scheme ([[def-group-scheme-over-a-scheme]]) whose generic fibre $G_K$ is an abelian variety ([[def-abelian-variety-over-a-field]]). Then
$$G^0=G_K\cup(G_k)^0$$
is an open $R$-subgroup scheme of $G$, smooth, separated and of finite type over $R$, with geometrically connected fibres. On each geometric fibre of $G$, the orbits of $G^0$ are exactly the connected components of that fibre.

references.title: Bosch, Lutkebohmert, Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 6.4 (identity components over a DVR)

items.title: Dilatations and defect computation
items.statement:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied algebra and scheme results. Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$, residue field $k$, uniformizer $\pi$, and let $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ be a strict henselization. Let $X$ be a finite-type flat $R$-scheme with smooth generic fibre of relative dimension $d$, and let $Y\subseteq X_k$ be a closed subscheme.

(a) The $\pi$-chart of the blowup $\operatorname{Bl}_Y(X)$ is flat over $R$ and universally receives a unique $R$-morphism over $X$ from every given $R$-morphism $B\to X$ with $B$ flat over $R$ whose special morphism $B_k\to X_k$ factors through $Y$; it is called the dilatation of $X$ along $Y$. Dilatations commute with unramified flat base change of DVRs and with products. A closed immersion $X_1\hookrightarrow X$ of flat $R$-schemes, with centre $Y_1=Y\times_X X_1$, induces a closed immersion of the corresponding dilatations; this is not a claim that arbitrary closed base change gives a cartesian square.

(b) For a section $a:\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$, the **defect** $\delta(a)$ is the length of the torsion submodule of $a^*\Omega_{X/R}$; it vanishes if and only if $X$ is smooth along $a$, and for smooth generic fibre it equals the minimum valuation of the maximal-rank Jacobian minors of a standard presentation of generic codimension, and is bounded uniformly over all $a\in X(R^{\mathrm{sh}})$.

(c) A morphism between smooth $R$-schemes of the same relative dimension is etale exactly at the points where its relative differential determinant is invertible; in particular $\delta(a)=0$ means that the special-fibre cotangent space at the rational specialization of $a$ has dimension $d$.

references.title: Bosch, Lutkebohmert, Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 2.2/8-10 and 3.2/1-2, 3.3/1-3 (dilatations and the defect of smoothness)

items.title: Affine codimension-one neighbourhoods and divisors
items.statement:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied algebra and scheme results.

(a) On a finite-type separated normal scheme over an affine Noetherian base, finitely many points of codimension at most one lie in a single affine open subscheme.

(b) For a normal Noetherian separated scheme $X$ and a dense affine open subscheme $U\subseteq X$, the complement $X\setminus U$ has pure codimension one in $X$; if $X$ is regular in addition, its reduced support is an effective Cartier divisor. If $X$ is flat over a discrete valuation ring and $U$ meets every irreducible component of the special fibre, then $X\setminus U$ is the closure of its generic fibre complement, so it contains no special-fibre component.

references.title: Bosch, Lutkebohmert, Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 6.4/4 and 6.5 condition (a); local proof in owner-arithmetic-models/neron-source/closure-supplement.md

items.title: Base change and products of abelian schemes
items.statement: Assume AC, inherited from smoothness and properness stability. Let $A\to S$ and $B\to S$ be abelian schemes of relative dimensions $g_A,g_B$ and let $S'\to S$ be a morphism. Then the base change $A_{S'}=A\times_SS'\to S'$ is an abelian scheme of relative dimension $g_A$, its $S'$-group structure is induced by that of $A$, and for every $s'\in S'$ with image $s\in S$ the fibre $(A_{S'})_{s'}$ is the base change $A_s\times_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(s')$ of abelian varieties. Likewise $A\times_SB\to S$ is an abelian scheme of relative dimension $g_A+g_B$ with the product group law. Kernels commute with arbitrary base change by their fibre-product definition; the base change of a finite locally free subgroup scheme is again such a subgroup, with the same rank. Scheme-theoretic images are not asserted to commute with arbitrary base change. The structural properties of an abelian scheme and geometric connectedness of fibres are preserved by base change; products have smooth proper geometrically connected fibres and the sum of the dimensions.

references.title: B. Edixhoven, G. van der Geer, B. Moonen, Abelian Varieties (preliminary version 2012), Chapter 6 sections 1-3

items.title: Weil's extension theorem for rational maps into smooth separated group schemes
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Dependent Choice, inherited from the descent and purity suppliers. Let $S$ be a regular Noetherian base scheme, let $Z$ be a smooth $S$-scheme, and let $G$ be a smooth separated $S$-group scheme of finite type. If an $S$-rational map $u:Z\dashrightarrow G$ is defined in codimension $\le1$, that is, at every height-one point of $Z$, then $u$ is defined everywhere and extends uniquely to an $S$-morphism $Z\to G$. Proof strategy (the regular-base specialization of BLR 4.4/1): let U be the domain of u and form v(z_1,z_2)=u(z_1)u(z_2)^{-1} on U×_S U. Near a hypothetical indeterminate point on the diagonal, use an affine neighbourhood H of the unit and the corrected affine-target lemma to obtain a pure codimension-one local indeterminacy locus. The diagonal exception lies in Z\U and therefore has codimension at least two. For the local diagonal contradiction, regularity of S and the published flat-local regularity ascent lemma show that Z and Z×_S Z have regular local rings: the fibre rings of a smooth map are geometrically regular. A pure codimension-one closed subset in such a local ring is the zero locus of a product f of finitely many irreducibles, by the published regular-local UFD theorem. Its restriction to the diagonal is a nonzero element, since the exceptional intersection has codimension at least two there, and is a nonunit if the point belongs to the intersection. The principal ideal theorem then gives a codimension-one component of that intersection, contradiction. This regular-base specialization of BLR 4.4/1 avoids an unproved general normal-base dimension assertion and suffices for every commissioned Dedekind/DVR consumer. On Z'=V∩(Z×_S U) the actual extension is v(z_1,z_2)u(z_2), not v alone. Smoothness makes pr_1 flat; each geometric fibre meets Z' since V contains the diagonal and U is fibrewise dense. It is therefore faithfully flat, and corrected morphism descent finishes the proof. Affine H is finite type over an affine base neighbourhood, as required by the corrected affine-target lemma.

references.title: Bosch, Lutkebohmert, Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 4.4/1 (Weil extension, regular base specialization)

items.title: Good reduction of an abelian variety over a Dedekind scheme
items.statement: Let $S$ be a Dedekind scheme with function field $K$, and let $A_K$ be an abelian variety over $K$. One says that $A_K$ has good reduction over $S$ if there exists an abelian scheme $A\to S$ together with an isomorphism $A\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K\cong A_K$. For a discrete valuation ring $R$ with fraction field $K$ this is the local notion; $A_K$ has potential good reduction if $A_K\otimes_KK'$ has good reduction over the normalization of $R$ in $K'$ for some finite extension $K'/K$. The reduction $A_s=A\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is an abelian variety over $\kappa(s)$. Good reduction is a property of the pair $(A_K,S)$; no claim is made that every abelian variety has good reduction.

references.title: J. S. Milne, Abelian Varieties, v2.00 (2008), Chapter I sections 3, 5, 8, 11, 17 (good reduction)
S. Bosch, W. Lutkebohmert, M. Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 1.2/8 and Chapter 7

items.title: The rigidified relative Picard functor and the dual abelian variety
items.statement: Let $f:A\to S$ be an abelian scheme with unit section $e:S\to A$. The rigidified relative Picard functor $\mathcal P_{A/S,e}$ is the fppf sheaf on $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)$ associated with the functor sending an $S$-scheme $T$ to the set of isomorphism classes of pairs $(\mathcal L,\alpha)$, where $\mathcal L$ is an invertible sheaf on $A_T$ and $\alpha:\mathcal O_T\to e_T^*\mathcal L$ is a trivialisation along the unit section, with group law given by tensor product. An $S$-scheme representing $\mathcal P_{A/S,e}$ is called a relative Picard scheme; its identity component is denoted $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{A/S}$ and, when it exists and is an abelian variety, is called the dual abelian variety $\hat A$ of $A$. A Poincare sheaf is the universal rigidified invertible sheaf $\mathcal P$ on $A\times_S\hat A$. The algebraically trivial subfunctor consists of classes whose geometric-fibre restrictions are algebraically equivalent to zero: algebraic equivalence is generated by differences of fibres in connected finite-type families of line bundles. This definition does not presuppose a representing scheme. Once a Picard scheme exists, the appropriate identity-component theorem identifies this subfunctor with Pic^0. The notation degree zero is not numerical degree on higher-dimensional A. For A/k the dual means a representing abelian variety for this subfunctor; representability and the Poincare sheaf remain claims of the commissioned theorem. No link from this definition to that later theorem is a dependency.

references.title: S. Bosch, W. Lutkebohmert, M. Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 8.1 (rigidified line bundles and the relative Picard functor)
B. Edixhoven, G. van der Geer, B. Moonen, Abelian Varieties (preliminary version 2012), Chapter 6 sections 1-3

items.title: Universal structure-sheaf sections of an abelian scheme
items.statement: Assume AC and DC as inherited from coherent cohomology and base change. Let f:A→S be an abelian scheme. For every T→S the unit map O_T→f_{T*}O_{A_T} is an isomorphism, and the inverse is evaluation along the identity section. Proof strategy: every geometric fibre is smooth, proper and connected, hence integral; its functions are scalars by thm-global-functions-proper-integral-variety. At every s the degree-zero fibre map is surjective since 1 lifts and spans H^0(A_s,O). On an affine base apply lem-proper-flat-fp-cohomology-perfect-complex to F=O_A, which is finitely presented and flat over the base; it need not be coherent when the base is noncoherent. Its nonnegative finite-projective complex and natural comparisons identify the degree-zero fibre map. Localize to a finite-free model and apply lem-cohomology-base-change-finite-free-criterion in degree zero: surjectivity gives universal base change and finite local freeness because the degree minus-one complex term vanishes. Thus the rank is one. The unit map is an isomorphism on fibres; in local bases it is multiplication by a unit, hence an isomorphism locally and globally. The identity section gives its inverse. The same argument applies to every base change, including nonreduced T; it does not infer morphism equality from geometric points.

references.title: J. S. Milne, Abelian Varieties, v2.00 (2008), Chapter I sections 3, 5, 8 (structure sheaf of an abelian scheme)

items.title: Prime to characteristic multiplication etale
items.statement:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the stated suppliers. if S is locally Noetherian, G/S is smooth, separated, commutative and finite type and n is invertible on S, [n]:G→G and G[n]→S are étale. Consequently G[n](Rsh)→G[n](ksep) is bijective. Proof strategy: Statement: if S is locally Noetherian, G/S is smooth, separated, commutative and finite type and n is invertible on S, [n]:G→G and G[n]→S are étale. Consequently G[n](Rsh)→G[n](ksep) is bijective.

Proof: on tangent spaces at the identity, the differential of [n] is n times the identity, by differentiating the sum of n copies of the identity group morphism. Translation identifies every other tangent differential with this one. On equal-dimensional smooth source/target charts the relative Jacobian criterion makes [n] étale wherever its differential is invertible. This fibrewise assertion plus the standard smooth local coordinates gives the assertion over R as well: the relative coordinate Jacobian has determinant a unit, so the graph equations present an étale morphism. Pull back along the identity to obtain G[n]; apply helper1. Negative n is handled by inversion. Source: BLR7.3/2(b), with its differential computation explicitly reproduced. Earlier supplier names for smooth Jacobian/base change: thm-jacobian-criterion-smooth-morphism; thm-ag-standard-smooth-base-change-composition; thm-etale-equivalent-flat-unramified-fp; lem-etale-residue-extensions-finite-separable. Parent must choose exact minimal graph against current definitions. This includes a field base, used by the Tate-module helper, and every strict henselian DVR base, used for specialization. The relative graph-Jacobian proof works over each affine open of S. The section-specialization consequence is asserted only in the DVR/strict-henselian setting.

references.title: Bosch, Lutkebohmert, Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 7.3/2(b) (multiplication by n prime to the residue characteristic)

items.title: Defect decrease and finite smoothening
items.statement:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied algebra and scheme results. Let R be a DVR, K its fraction field, k its residue field, and Rsh a chosen strict henselization. In clauses involving A, let A/K be the given abelian variety. If Y has schematically dense liftable ks-points and U in Y is smooth with OmegaX/R restricted locally free, dilatation lowers positive defect by at least one for every section specializing in U. For X separated flat and finite type over any DVR with smooth generic fibre there is a finite sequence of special-fibre blowups, proper and generically identical, whose smooth locus contains every Rsh-section. Complete proof strategy: Choose smooth ambient Z and coordinates y,z with Y=(pi,z). Vanishing differentials and density of liftable points show Id(X) is contained in (pi,z)^2. Substitute z=pi zprime and divide equations by pi squared; each relevant Jacobian column gains a negative pi power, so minors decrease in valuation. Source locators: BLR 3.3/5; BLR 3.4/1–2; 3.1/3–4. Stratify the closure of specializations by smooth/free loci. Blow up the deepest stratum first, decrease its defect, and use induction on bounded defect and finite stratum length. Do not assert all nested strata are simultaneously permissible: only the deepest current stratum is used. Source locators: BLR 3.3/5; BLR 3.4/1–2; 3.1/3–4. For a centre Y with schematically dense ks-points, each affine coordinate ring B injects into a product of copies of ks via evaluation. This remains injective after tensoring with an arbitrary field extension l/k: every relation uses finitely many coefficients, and on their finite-dimensional k-span tensoring commutes with the coordinate evaluations. Since ks is separable algebraic over k, each ks tensor l is reduced; therefore B tensor l is reduced. This proves geometric reduction rather than merely reduction over ks.

To prove dense smoothness, extend to a perfect closure of k. The scheme remains reduced. At each generic point its function field is separably generated over that perfect field (`thm-ag-separating-transcendence-basis-perfect-field`); `thm-ag-field-differentials-separable-rank` gives differential rank equal to transcendence degree. The relative Jacobian criterion and actual defining ideal produce a smooth neighbourhood of that generic point, as in the ambient comparison above. Smoothness descends through field extension by the exact `lem-ag-geometric-regularity-field-tests`, flatness over a field and the smoothness criterion. Thus the original smooth locus is dense. A coherent sheaf is free on a dense open of each reduced component: choose a basis over its fraction field, clear denominators in finitely many generators and relations, then remove the other components and intersect the finitely many resulting opens. Alternatively `lem-generic-freeness-finite-type-algebra-module` supplies this exact step with B=A and M the coherent module. For this local packet the smoothening assertions are restricted to separated flat finite-type R-models with smooth generic fibre; the commissioned projective generic closures and their blowups satisfy flatness (chart rings are R-torsion-free). The broader source theorem for arbitrary nonflat R-schemes is unnecessary and is not used.

references.title: Bosch, Lutkebohmert, Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 3.3/5 and 3.4/1-2 (finite permissible smoothening)

items.title: K-morphisms from smooth models into abelian schemes extend uniquely
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Let $S$ be a Dedekind scheme with function field $K$, let $A\to S$ be an abelian scheme, and let $Z\to S$ be a smooth $S$-scheme of finite type. Then restriction along $Z_K=Z\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K\hookrightarrow Z$ is a bijection $$\operatorname{Hom}_S(Z,A)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_K(Z_K,A_K).$$ In particular, for every closed point $s\in S$ and every generic point $\xi$ of the fibre $Z_s$ the local ring $\mathcal O_{Z,\xi}$ is a discrete valuation ring whose fraction field is the function field of the irreducible component of $Z$ containing $\xi$, a field containing $K$; a given $K$-morphism $Z_K\to A_K$ therefore yields a $K(Z)$-point of $A$, and the valuative criterion of properness for $A/S$ extends it over $\mathcal O_{Z,\xi}$; it is therefore defined in codimension $\le1$, and Weil's extension theorem applies. This is the extension statement used to identify abelian schemes as Neron models. Work componentwise because a smooth scheme over a Dedekind base is regular and its components are disjoint locally. The generic fibre lies in the initial domain, and every remaining height-one point is a generic point of a special fibre. After the valuative lift, finite presentation of A and Z spreads the local-ring morphism to a neighbourhood; then apply the corrected Weil extension strategy. Non-finite-type smooth sources are handled by an open cover by finite-type smooth subschemes, with the extensions glued uniquely.

references.title: Bosch, Lutkebohmert, Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 4.4/4 (extension of K-morphisms into abelian schemes)

items.title: The theorem of the square and the Mumford homomorphism into the Picard group
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $A$ be an abelian variety over a field $k$, let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible sheaf on $A$, and let $t_a:A\to A$ denote translation by $a\in A(k'')$ for a field extension $k''/k$. Then the theorem of the square holds: $$t_{a+b}^*\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal L\;\cong\;t_a^*\mathcal L\otimes t_b^*\mathcal L$$ for all $a,b\in A(k'')$, and the formula is functorial in $k''$. Consequently the Mumford map $$\varphi_{\mathcal L}:A(k'')\longrightarrow\operatorname{Pic}(A_{k''}),\qquad a\longmapsto[t_a^*\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal L^{-1}],$$ is a homomorphism of groups and lands in the degree-zero part of the rigidified Picard functor; it is compatible with field extension. The proof derives the square formula by specialising the published theorem of the cube to the three maps $1_A,a,b:A\to A$, exactly as in Milne I.5.5-I.5.6.

references.title: J. S. Milne, Abelian Varieties, v2.00 (2008), I.5.5-I.5.6 (theorem of the square)

items.title: Fibrewise constant morphisms from an abelian scheme factor through the base
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Let A→S be an abelian scheme, T→S any morphism and Z any scheme. If u:A_T→Z sends each geometric fibre over T to a single point, then u=u∘e_T∘f_T as scheme morphisms. Proof strategy: for t∈T choose an affine open W of Z containing the image point of the fibre. Properness of f_T makes the image of u^{-1}(Z\W) closed and disjoint from t. Choose an affine neighbourhood V=Spec R of t avoiding it. Then u|_{A_V} lands in W=Spec B. The preceding universal-sections lemma gives Γ(A_V,O)=R, so the ring map B→Γ(A_V,O) defines a map V→W and u factors through it. Evaluation along e identifies the factor with u∘e. These factorizations agree on overlaps and cover T. This proof controls nilpotents; fibrewise equality alone would not.

references.title: J. S. Milne, Abelian Varieties, v2.00 (2008), Chapter I sections 3, 5, 8 (rigidity)

items.title: Field prime to characteristic torsion and tate module
items.statement:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the stated suppliers. for A/F abelian dimension g and prime ell≠char F, A[ell^v](Fsep)≅(Z/ell^v)^(2g), multiplication by ell gives surjective transition maps, and T_ell A≅Z_ell^(2g). The natural projections give T_ell A/ell^v T_ell A≅A[ell^v](Fsep). Inertia acts trivially on T iff it acts trivially on every finite torsion group. Proof strategy: Statement: for A/F abelian dimension g and prime ell≠char F, A[ell^v](Fsep)≅(Z/ell^v)^(2g), multiplication by ell gives surjective transition maps, and T_ell A≅Z_ell^(2g). The natural projections give T_ell A/ell^v T_ell A≅A[ell^v](Fsep). Inertia acts trivially on T iff it acts trivially on every finite torsion group.

Exact supplier: thm-nonaffine-abelian-multiplication-finite-faithfully-flat supplies finite locally free [n] and rank |n|^(2g) over arbitrary fields, including surjectivity on algebraically closed points. Helper2 gives étaleness, so separable geometric points have cardinal ell^(2gv). For a finite abelian ell-group H=A[ell^v], H[ell]=A[ell] has ell^(2g) elements; elementary cyclic classification says H has 2g cyclic factors, each exponent at most v. Since the sum of their exponents is 2gv, every exponent is v. Roots for each torsion point exist by field multiplication, and roots of ell^v-torsion are ell^(v+1)-torsion. Lift a basis recursively; the lifts are independent because reducing any relation by ell gives divisibility of every coefficient by ell^v, after which cardinality/order settles independence. Compatible coordinates yield the Z_ell basis of the inverse limit. For the quotient assertion, if a compatible sequence has vth coordinate zero, define b_r=a_(r+v), viewed in A[ell^r] since ell^r a_(r+v)=a_v=0; then ell^v b=a. Projection is onto by recursive root lifting. Thus the kernel is ell^v T. Inertia equivalence follows from these quotients and coordinatewise equality. This is an elementary group argument after the exact multiplication supplier; no H1 duality assertion is made. All necessary choice assumptions from that supplier persist.

references.title: J. S. Milne, Abelian Varieties, v2.00 (2008), Chapter I sections 11 and 17 (Tate modules)

items.title: Projective weak models and rational mapping
items.statement:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied algebra and scheme results. Let R be a DVR, K its fraction field, k its residue field, and Rsh a chosen strict henselization. In clauses involving A, let A/K be the given abelian variety. For every abelian A/K and arbitrary DVR R there is a smooth separated finite-type model V with V(Rsh)=A(Ksh). A weak model collection for A receives every generic rational map from smooth Z/R with irreducible special fibre as an R-rational map. Weak models remain weak after R to O_Z,eta at a special-fibre generic point. Complete proof strategy: Embed A in projective space using the published projectivity theorem; take its schematic closure over R. Proper valuative lifting gives all Ksh-points, and P04 then its smooth locus gives V. No excellence, bounded-model theorem or flattening is needed. Source locators: BLR 3.1 final paragraph; 3.5 first paragraph; BLR 3.5/3–4. Close graphs; lift dense special rational points to sections over Rsh and use the weak property to cover them. Constructibility forces some graph image to contain the generic special point. A local ring dominating that DVR with the same fraction field equals it; spread the isomorphism. Etale neighbourhood limits give base change. Source locators: BLR 3.1 final paragraph; 3.5 first paragraph; BLR 3.5/3–4. Use relative fibre-dense opens, not arbitrary absolute dense opens, for the birational functor. On a smooth scheme over a DVR, a fibre-dense open meets every generic point of the regular total space and is schematically dense. This remains true after the flat base changes actually used. For arbitrary base changes in strict-law functor calculations, smoothness gives geometrically reduced fibres and flatness; the affine associated-prime calculation in BLR 2.5/1(b) proves universal schematic density. For a separated target, local representatives agree by the closed diagonal and schematic density and glue to the maximal domain.

The graph closure of a rational map is calculated on a finite affine cover by kernels of restriction maps. Flat tensor products preserve those kernels and finite equalizers; hence graph closure commutes with flat base change. The domain is exactly the open where graph projection is an isomorphism. If a faithfully flat pullback of that projection is an isomorphism, affine ring descent gives an isomorphism before pullback. Thus domains descend through faithfully flat source maps and commute with flat base changes, exactly BLR 2.5/5–6. The target-separated hypothesis is essential. For maps between Noetherian finite-type schemes, finite presentation spreads the stalk statement; the explicit spreading computation is given below. This is sufficient for the separated smooth graph and completion applications and the tensor-product bases in the completion cocycle. Published `thm-affine-blowup-standard-charts` and `lem-affine-blowup-algebra-properties` give the actual chart algebra A[I/pi] as the quotient of A[tj]/(pi tj-gj) by pi-power torsion. Thus the dilatation chart is flat over the DVR. The Rees-Proj construction is proper by `thm-blowup-projective`; centres contain pi so the generic fibre is unchanged. For a flat source B, the special-factorization condition makes each gj image divisible by pi, uniquely. Sending tj to gj/pi kills all torsion and proves the universal property. Flat base change preserves the relevant torsion-free chart description by tensoring the finite kernel/equalizer or by this universal property; products and closed immersions follow by the same universal property and affine coordinate equations. Unique section lifting under the proper blowup follows from the exact `thm-valuative-criterion-properness`.

The essential finite-stage stalk argument is explicit. Suppose A and B are finite-type R-domains in a common field L, A included in B, and Ap=Bq via the map at p,q. Write B=A[b1,...,bm]. Each bj is aj/sj in Ap. Taking s the product of sj, outside p, gives Bs=As as subrings of L. Consequently Spec Bs to Spec As is an isomorphism on neighbourhoods of q,p. This applies to generic graph projections, since graph closures are integral and have the same generic fraction field. For finite-presentation schemes over a filtered colimit ring, choose finite affine covers and finite covers of their overlaps, record the finitely many equations, generators, gluing maps and inverse identities. All these coefficients occur at one finite stage; finitely many equality identities hold at a later common stage. This proves the object/morphism spreading used for etale neighbourhood limits. Generic closure over a DVR is pi-torsion-free by its kernel definition, hence flat. 

For the universal schematic-density step, the associated-prime calculation can be proved locally, rather than treating BLR's EGA reference as a supplier. Over a Noetherian base ring C, take a finite prime filtration of C (`thm-prime-filtration-of-a-finite-module`) and tensor with the flat smooth algebra B. The resulting filtration of B has factors B/pB. Each factor is flat over the domain C/p, so injects into its generic fibre. That generic fibre is geometrically reduced, hence reduced; consequently B/pB is reduced. A reduced Noetherian ring has only minimal associated primes: it injects into the finite product of its minimal-prime domain quotients, and the annihilator of any element is the intersection of the minimal primes where its image is nonzero; a prime such intersection equals one of them. The associated primes of B are therefore contained in the union of the minimal primes of these factors. Each such factor-minimal prime lies over p: flatness prevents a nonzero C/p element from being a zero divisor. A fibre-dense open meets all of these generic fibre-component points. The kernel of restriction to that open, if nonzero, has an associated prime by `thm-existence-of-associated-primes`; as a submodule of B this prime is one of the just listed primes, where restriction is injective, contradiction. Thus restriction is injective. After an arbitrary affine base change, write its base ring as the filtered colimit of finite-type algebras over the original DVR. Each stage is Noetherian, and the open remains fibre-dense by geometric density over field extension. Restriction injectivity passes to the colimit by exactness of filtered colimits and the finite affine-cover equalizer. This supplies universal schematic density for the arbitrary T-valued strict-law calculations.

references.title: Bosch, Lutkebohmert, Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 3.1 final paragraph and 3.5/3-4 (projective weak models and rational mapping); proof closure in owner-arithmetic-models/neron-source/closure-supplement.md

items.title: Rigidification and effective descent of line bundles
items.statement:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied scheme and cohomology results. For an abelian variety A/k with identity e, the rigidified line-bundle functor is an fppf sheaf on all k-schemes. Rigidified bundles have no nontrivial automorphisms; normalization L↦L⊗p_T^*e_T^*L^{-1} identifies its classes with Pic(A_T)/Pic(T). Complete proof strategy: 

Work first over an algebraically closed field. For proper geometrically integral A, universal constants satisfy p_*O_(A×T)=O_T for every T. On affine tests, compute by a finite affine Čech cover and tensor the field cohomology complex; H0 is k. Normalize L by tensoring with p_T^*(e_T^*L)^−1. A rigidified line bundle has no nontrivial automorphism, since each automorphism is a unit from T and restriction along e determines it. Thus isomorphisms on an fppf overlap are unique and satisfy the cocycle; effective module descent gives a line bundle with rigidification. Consequently the rigidified functor is already an fppf sheaf, without invoking representability.

references.title: S. Bosch, Lutkebohmert, Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 8.1 (rigidified line bundles and fppf descent)

items.title: Fibres of abelian schemes and unit-preserving morphisms
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $S$ be a scheme, let $A\to S$ and $B\to S$ be abelian schemes of relative dimensions $g_A,g_B$, and let $s\in S$. Then the fibre $A_s$ is an abelian variety of dimension $g_A$ over $\kappa(s)$; the multiplication of $A$ is commutative; the inversion of $A$ is the morphism $-1_A:A\to A$; and every $S$-morphism $u:A\to B$ with $u\circ e_A=e_B$ is a homomorphism of $S$-group schemes. Consequently, on a connected base, any two abelian-scheme structures on the same smooth proper $S$-scheme with the same unit section coincide. For commutativity, fix the second variable and apply the new fibrewise-constant rigidity lemma to the commutator map A×_S A→A: on each geometric fibre of the second projection the field-level commutativity theorem makes it constant at the identity, and evaluation at the first identity gives zero over the entire base. This proves equality as morphisms, including nilpotents. With commutativity established, apply the same lemma to the defect u(a+b)-u(a)-u(b), whose geometric fibres in the first variable are constant zero by the field pointed-morphism theorem. Evaluation at a=0 makes the factor identically zero. For uniqueness apply this homomorphism result to the identity morphism between the two structures.
