items.title: Polarizations and the Mumford isogeny attached to an ample line bundle
items.statement: Let A/k be an abelian variety and suppose a dual abelian variety A^vee with its universal normalized Poincare bundle P has been supplied. For a line bundle L on A the Mumford morphism phi_L is represented by the family Lambda(L)=m^*L⊗p_1^*L^{-1}⊗p_2^*L^{-1}⊗π^*e^*L on A×A, rigidified along both identity factors. Thus (id_A×phi_L)^*P≅Lambda(L); the map used here has domain A×A. A polarization is a homomorphism lambda:A→A^vee for which after extension to an algebraic closure there is an ample line bundle L with lambda=phi_L. A principal polarization is a polarization of degree one, where the degree is the finite locally free rank of the associated isogeny. Symmetry lambda=lambda^vee under the bidual identification, finiteness/isogeny, existence of the dual, and existence and square degree of polarizations are conclusions to prove in the subsequent commissioned theorem; they are not assumed as existence assertions by this definition. Defining the conditional terms does not create a dependency from this definition back to that theorem.

references.title: J. S. Milne, Abelian Varieties, v2.00 (2008), Chapter I sections 5 and 8, and Chapter III (polarizations)
B. Edixhoven, G. van der Geer, B. Moonen, Abelian Varieties (preliminary version 2012), Chapter 6 sections 1-3

items.title: Special fibre torsion growth detects properness
items.statement:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the stated suppliers. for smooth commutative finite-type G/k, dim G=g, if |G[ell^v](kbar)|=ell^(2gv) for every v≥1, then G^0 is an abelian variety. Proof strategy: Statement: for smooth commutative finite-type G/k, dim G=g, if |G[ell^v](kbar)|=ell^(2gv) for every v≥1, then G^0 is an abelian variety.

Exact supplier: thm-barsotti-chevalley-perfect-field-group-variety applied over kbar; helper3 for abelian torsion count; helper4 for affine torsion bound. Write 0→N→G^0→B→0 with dimN=a and dimB=b, so g=a+b. Every torsion fibre over B[ell^v] contains at most |N[ell^v]| points, by subtracting any point in that fibre. Therefore |G^0[ell^v]|≤ell^(v(2b+a)). There are C finitely many components; subtracting a torsion point in a component injects that component's torsion into G^0[ell^v], hence |G[ell^v]|≤C ell^(v(2g-a)). The assumed cardinal forces ell^(va)≤C for all v, so a=0. The affine smooth connected N is then trivial, hence G^0=B. A purely inseparable ksep→kbar extension changes no points of the étale finite torsion scheme: its residue extensions are finite separable, and ksep is separably closed. Properness descends along the algebraic closure, giving abelian G^0/k. Exact geometric properness descent supplier: lem-nonaffine-geometric-properness-field-descent. This bound suffices for NOS and avoids asserting the stronger exact exponent 2b+t.

references.title: Bosch, Lutkebohmert, Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 7.4 (component growth and properness detection); proof in owner-arithmetic-models/etale-source/closure-packet.md

items.title: Invariant volume and finite minimal classes
items.statement:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied algebra and scheme results. Let R be a DVR, K its fraction field, k its residue field, and Rsh a chosen strict henselization. In clauses involving A, let A/K be the given abelian variety. A smooth d-dimensional group has a nowhere-vanishing invariant top form. On a smooth model with irreducible special fibre pi to minus ord times the form extends to a generator. A rational generically identical map between smooth irreducible-special-fibre models satisfies ordsource>=ordtarget; equality makes it an open immersion on its domain. Orders have a finite minimum and there are finitely many equivalence classes of minimal models. Minimal representatives after R to O_Z,eta remain minimal and cover all minimal equivalence classes after splitting special components. Complete proof strategy: Translate the cotangent space at the identity to trivialize Omega. Extend pi-normalized generic section through codimension one by Hartogs and rule out zeros by pure codimension-one support. For A, left and right invariance agree by published commutativity, so the general bounded modular-character argument is unnecessary. Source locators: BLR 4.2/1–3; 4.3 initial paragraphs; BLR 4.3/1–2; BLR 4.3/3. Pull back normalized volume; its scalar coefficient is pi to the order difference times a unit. Nonnegative order gives inequality, zero order gives etaleness. Apply P06 to a finite weak collection; its minimum bounds every model, and a minimal model is birationally equivalent to one of the finitely many minimal members. Source locators: BLR 4.2/1–3; 4.3 initial paragraphs; BLR 4.3/1–2; BLR 4.3/3. The base-changed weak collection remains weak by P06, and the normalized volume order at each special generic point is unchanged. Repeat the finite-minimum argument over the new DVR. Source locators: BLR 4.2/1–3; 4.3 initial paragraphs; BLR 4.3/1–2; BLR 4.3/3. The exact published smoothness criterion gives flatness and geometric regular fibres. `lem-ag-flat-local-regularity-ascent-descent` then gives regular local rings of every smooth DVR total space. `thm-nonaffine-regular-local-ring-is-ufd` applies to **every regular local ring**, including these total spaces; its subsequent field example does not restrict that first assertion. Thus their Weil divisors are locally Cartier and extend generic Cartier divisors by closing their prime supports. The rational section correspondence is precisely `thm-line-bundle-rational-section-cartier-divisor`.

Here is the required scheme Hartogs proof. Let A be a Noetherian normal domain and a/b a fraction outside A. The nonzero cyclic submodule generated by a modulo b in A/bA has an associated prime p, by `thm-existence-of-associated-primes` (AC implies its DC assumption). Then (A/bA)p has depth zero. Since b is regular, `lem-depth-quotient-by-regular-element` gives depth Ap equal to one. Normality implies S2 by `lem-normal-domain-implies-s-two`, so height p is at most one. It cannot be zero since b belongs to p. Moreover a/b remains outside Ap: localizing its nonzero cyclic module at its associated prime does not kill it. This proves A is the intersection of its height-one localizations. Apply it to coefficients in a local frame to extend a line-bundle section defined in codimension one. A nonzero section's zero set has pure codimension one because locally it is a nonzero principal element in a regular domain.

For a separated quasi-finite birational morphism Y to a normal integral X with Y reduced, apply `lem-scheme-zariski-main-factorization-quasi-finite` locally to get an open immersion into a finite X-scheme. Take the reduced closure of the generic Y image in that finite scheme. Its affine ring B is integral over A and embeds in Frac A; normality forces B=A. The open Y image lies in this closure because Y is reduced and its generic point is dense. Therefore Y to X is an open immersion. The published classical-variety-only finite-birational result is not used. The order comparison applies also to a generic isomorphism preserving the invariant top form, not only the generic identity. Left and right translations on the abelian generic fibre preserve that form, so the comparison applies to the translation steps used by the next helper.

references.title: Bosch, Lutkebohmert, Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 4.2/1-3 and 4.3 (invariant volume, comparison, finite minimal classes)

items.title: Cube-derived square over DVR
items.statement:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied algebra and scheme results. Let R be a DVR, K its fraction field, k its residue field, and Rsh a chosen strict henselization. In clauses involving A, let A/K be the given abelian variety. For A/K abelian and every line bundle L, the square obstruction on A times A times A is pulled back from the first two A factors. For H smooth separated finite type over a DVR with abelian generic fibre, and H0 its identity component, every line bundle on H satisfies the square for the H0 translation action. For a smooth finite-type group scheme over a DVR the fibrewise identity components form an open subgroup G0 with geometrically connected fibres; its orbits on the trivial torsor are geometric connected components. Complete proof strategy: Rewrite the cube identity as L(x+y+z)L(z)/(L(x+z)L(y+z)) = L(x+y)/(L(x)L(y)), up to constant identity-fibre factors. This is a literal line-bundle pullback identity. No Picard representability, dual abelian variety, or Poincare bundle is used. Source locators: Published cube supplier; BLR 6.3 introductory classical case; BLR 6.3/2 abelian generic specialization. Extend the generic base line bundle on H0 times H0 by regular divisor closure. The residual square obstruction is vertical. Since H0 has geometrically irreducible fibres, its vertical divisor on H0 times H0 times H is pulled back from H. Pull back along (unit,unit,idH) to identify that line bundle with one pulled back from R, then absorb it in the base line bundle. Source locators: Published cube supplier; BLR 6.3 introductory classical case; BLR 6.3/2 abelian generic specialization. Construct component neighbourhoods etale locally and descend the component containing the unit; on each geometric fibre translate the identity component. Source locator: BLR 6.4 pre-Lemma3; EGA IV 15.6.5 prerequisite not fully read. 

In the square reduction, the residual obstruction line bundle on G0 times G0 times G has a vertical divisor. Projection to G has geometrically integral fibres on the special fibre, so each vertical prime divisor upstairs is the inverse image of a special component of G. Thus it is pulled back from G. Restrict to (unit,unit,idG): the square obstruction becomes trivial there and the extended generic base line bundle pulls back from R. This identifies the residual G line bundle with one from R, which can be absorbed in the G0 times G0 base line bundle. The generic cube identity is the exact published cube theorem. No Picard scheme, dual abelian variety, Chevalley decomposition or Raynaud theorem is used.

references.title: Bosch, Lutkebohmert, Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 6.3 (the square from the cube, abelian generic fibre)

items.title: Divisor charts and the separated rigidified Picard diagonal
items.statement:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied scheme and cohomology results. For projective geometrically integral A/k, sufficiently positive relative effective Cartier divisors with fixed Hilbert polynomial form a finite-type open Hilbert chart D. Its class map to the Picard fppf sheaf is relatively a smooth projective-space bundle over the appropriate open positive-class subfunctor, on arbitrary tests. The diagonal of that sheaf is represented and separated; after representability the Picard scheme is separated. Complete proof strategy: Fix a very ample line bundle H on A. The relative effective-divisor functor is an open of the published Hilbert scheme: on a flat finitely presented family, being cut out by a fibrewise regular element with invertible ideal is open, by the local flatness criterion plus Nakayama and proper projection of the bad locus. For a fixed Hilbert polynomial, this divisor scheme D is finite type and quasi-projective. Use positive charts with a specified Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity bound: impose the finitely many higher-cohomology vanishings in that regularity definition, using the universal finite cohomology complex. The published relative-regularity/base-change supplier propagates these finitely many vanishings to all required nonnegative twists. After twisting by a sufficiently high H power every individual test family is locally on its base in such a chart, by Serre vanishing. The chosen chart is an open D^+, with fixed polynomial and fixed finite regularity conditions; do not define openness by an unproved infinite intersection of vanishings. A line bundle satisfying these conditions has finite locally free sections, compatible with every base change, with positive rank.

 The map D^+ to the line-bundle sheaf is relatively represented by projective spaces: for an arbitrary test family L, divisors with class L are fibrewise nonzero sections up to units from the test base. Integral fibres make every nonzero fibre section regular. Hence the fibre is P((p_*L)^∨), scheme theoretically, and is smooth projective surjective. The linear-equivalence relation R on D^+ is therefore a represented smooth projective relation, of finite type, with both projections flat. Its map to D^+×D^+ is a monomorphism. The source is separated and finite type, so the published generic quotient theorem applies exactly, yielding a nonempty saturated open W and Y=W/R_W.

 Separatedness can be checked on these locally finite-type charts. If a rigidified line bundle on A_R, for a DVR R over the field, is trivial generically, its Cartier divisor is supported on the irreducible special fibre of the smooth regular A_R. On a regular scheme Cartier and Weil divisors agree, and this divisor is an integer multiple of the special fibre, the principal divisor of the uniformizer. Thus its class is trivial modulo a base line bundle. For diagonal representability and quasi-compactness, on the Noetherian product T of two finite-type divisor charts put M=L1^−1⊗L2 with the prescribed rigidification. A universal finite free cohomology complex has H0(M_T′)=ker(d0:K0⊗OT′→K1⊗OT′) on every test. Evaluation at the unit is a linear functional on this kernel; choosing a free representative of the degree-zero evaluation chain map gives its linear extension to K0. Sections with d0(s)=0 and e(s)=1 are therefore represented by a closed subscheme of the finite-rank affine vector bundle K0, defined by finitely many linear equations. Restrict to the open where the section is invertible everywhere on A: the zero locus of the universal section is closed, and its proper image in the parameter scheme is closed. This open is Noetherian, finite type, and quasi-compact. Such sections are exactly rigidified isomorphisms L1→L2, uniquely if they exist. Thus the diagonal is representable and quasi-compact on these covering chart products. The Noetherian DVR valuative uniqueness criterion now gives separatedness. Chain evaluation can be constructed by an affine Čech model and transferred to the finite projective complex; this should be written explicitly in authoring.

 The universal Hilbert ideal is flat over its Noetherian chart base because both the structure sheaf and universal flat quotient are base-flat. On a fibre where the ideal is a line bundle, the Noetherian fibrewise-flatness criterion makes it flat over the target local ring, and the finite-flat local freeness criterion makes it rank one. The locus is open; proper projection of its failure gives the divisor open in the Hilbert chart. Arbitrary test families descend locally to finitely generated k-algebras by finite-presentation spreading of the line bundle and its inverse, so these representing opens and linear-system universal properties apply to every test.

For general projective geometrically integral A, the Picard fppf sheaf is the sheafification of T↦Pic(A_T)/p_T^*Pic(T). Rigidification is used only after a rational section e is supplied; normalization then identifies this sheaf with e-rigidified classes. A finite separable extension supplies a rational point of the smooth locus when needed, and the affine diagonal descends by affine algebra descent. The separatedness proof uses inverse sections and the integral special fibre, so it does not require A to be smooth or regular.

references.title: B. Edixhoven, G. van der Geer, B. Moonen, Abelian Varieties (2012), Chapters 2-3, 6-9, 11 (relative divisors and the Picard scheme); closure in owner-arithmetic-models/dual-source/proof-closure-packet.md
S. Kleiman, The Picard Scheme, Theorem 4.8 divisor-chart proof (quotient step replaced locally by the published generic quotient)

items.title: Multiplication by n on an abelian scheme is finite flat, and etale for n invertible
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Dependent Choice, inherited from the finite-flatness and flatness-by-fibres suppliers. Let $S$ be locally Noetherian and let $A\to S$ be an abelian scheme of relative dimension $g$, let $n\ge1$, and let $[n]:A\to A$ be multiplication by $n$. Then $[n]$ is finite, flat and surjective of degree $n^{2g}$, and the kernel $A[n]=\ker[n]$ is a finite flat $S$-group scheme of rank $n^{2g}$. If $n$ is invertible on $S$, then $[n]$ is etale and $A[n]\to S$ is finite etale of rank $n^{2g}$. The proof is fibrewise: on every geometric fibre $[n]$ has finite kernel of order $n^{2g}$ by the published field-level theorem, so $[n]$ is quasi-finite and proper, hence finite, and flatness follows by applying lem-noetherian-flatness-by-fibres-finite-target-module to the local tower O_{S,s}→O_{A,y}→O_{A,x} for [n], with M=O_{A,x}: smoothness makes M flat over O_{S,s}, and the published field-level multiplication theorem makes its special-fibre module flat over the special-fibre target. Constancy of the rank then follows from the field rank n^{2g}; etaleness follows because the differential of $[n]$ at the unit is multiplication by the invertible scalar $n$ on the locally free sheaf of invariant differentials, and translations spread this everywhere.

references.title: J. S. Milne, Abelian Varieties, v2.00 (2008), Chapter I sections 3, 5, 8 (multiplication by n)

items.title: An abelian scheme is the Neron model of its generic fibre
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Let $S$ be a Dedekind scheme with function field $K$ and let $A\to S$ be an abelian scheme. Then $A$ is a Neron model of its generic fibre $A_K$: for every smooth $S$-scheme $Y$ and every $K$-morphism $u_K:Y_K\to A_K$ there is a unique $S$-morphism $Y\to A$ extending $u_K$. Proof strategy (BLR 1.2/8): fix a closed point $s\in S$ and a generic point $\xi$ of the fibre $Y_s$; then $\mathcal O_{Y,\xi}$ is a discrete valuation ring whose fraction field is the function field $K(Y)$, a field containing $K$, the given $K$-morphism yields a $K(Y)$-point of $A$, and the valuative criterion of properness for the proper morphism $A\to S$ extends it over $\xi$. Hence the resulting $S$-rational map is defined in codimension $\le1$ and Weil's extension theorem makes it a morphism; uniqueness is separatedness of $A$. This directly proves the full mapping property. The weak mapping property is a consequence and is not used to upgrade it; such an upgrade would require a group scheme on the model and the independent weak mapping theorem.

references.title: S. Bosch, W. Lutkebohmert, M. Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 1.2/8 (an abelian scheme is a Neron model of its generic fibre)

items.title: Separated minimal union and translations
items.statement:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied algebra and scheme results. Let R be a DVR, K its fraction field, k its residue field, and Rsh a chosen strict henselization. In clauses involving A, let A/K be the given abelian variety. There exists a smooth separated finite-type faithfully flat model X of A formed by gluing finitely many minimal representatives along A. Every translation by a point over a generic smooth-DVR extension extends to a birational open immersion. Complete proof strategy: Close pairwise generic diagonals. If a special projection is dominant, a DVR dominance argument gives birational equivalence, contradicting distinct classes. Remove the nowhere-dense images to ensure separated gluing. Apply P06 and order minimality to a translation and its inverse. Source locators: BLR 4.3/4. Published `thm-affine-blowup-standard-charts` and `lem-affine-blowup-algebra-properties` give the actual chart algebra A[I/pi] as the quotient of A[tj]/(pi tj-gj) by pi-power torsion. Thus the dilatation chart is flat over the DVR. The Rees-Proj construction is proper by `thm-blowup-projective`; centres contain pi so the generic fibre is unchanged. For a flat source B, the special-factorization condition makes each gj image divisible by pi, uniquely. Sending tj to gj/pi kills all torsion and proves the universal property. Flat base change preserves the relevant torsion-free chart description by tensoring the finite kernel/equalizer or by this universal property; products and closed immersions follow by the same universal property and affine coordinate equations. Unique section lifting under the proper blowup follows from the exact `thm-valuative-criterion-properness`.

The essential finite-stage stalk argument is explicit. Suppose A and B are finite-type R-domains in a common field L, A included in B, and Ap=Bq via the map at p,q. Write B=A[b1,...,bm]. Each bj is aj/sj in Ap. Taking s the product of sj, outside p, gives Bs=As as subrings of L. Consequently Spec Bs to Spec As is an isomorphism on neighbourhoods of q,p. This applies to generic graph projections, since graph closures are integral and have the same generic fraction field. For finite-presentation schemes over a filtered colimit ring, choose finite affine covers and finite covers of their overlaps, record the finitely many equations, generators, gluing maps and inverse identities. All these coefficients occur at one finite stage; finitely many equality identities hold at a later common stage. This proves the object/morphism spreading used for etale neighbourhood limits. Generic closure over a DVR is pi-torsion-free by its kernel definition, hence flat.

references.title: Bosch, Lutkebohmert, Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 4.3/4 (separated minimal union and translations)

items.title: Divisor ampleness
items.statement:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied algebra and scheme results. Let R be a DVR, K its fraction field, k its residue field, and Rsh a chosen strict henselization. In clauses involving A, let A/K be the given abelian variety. For every smooth separated finite-type R-group scheme H with abelian generic fibre, every effective divisor D whose complement is affine and fibre-dense gives ample O(D). On a qcqs scheme, a finite cover by quasi-affine nonvanishing loci of sections of positive powers characterizes ampleness. Ampleness of a given line bundle descends fpqc. An ample line bundle with compatible fpqc descent datum makes scheme descent effective. In particular every such smooth separated finite-type R-group scheme H with abelian generic fibre is quasi-projective over R: choose the R-dense affine open supplied by the codimension-one neighbourhood lemma, take its effective horizontal Cartier boundary D, and O(D) is ample by the orbit/square argument. A finite affine-section chart construction, given below, gives a locally closed projective-space embedding; the proper-source very-ample theorem is not applied to H. Complete proof strategy: Fibre-density means complement meets every H0 orbit. Over a strict henselization, the square implies Dg+Dg inverse is linearly equivalent to 2D. The associated sections have quasi-affine nonvanishing loci gU intersect g inverse U. These cover H: suitable g occur in a dense open in each H0 fibre and hence among sections. Apply quasi-affine-locus ampleness criterion and descend the same line bundle. Source locators: BLR 6.4/2–3 specialized to trivial torsor. Use the section ring Proj or affine refinements of quasi-affine loci; descend the graded algebra by module descent and cover by nonvanishing loci of descended sections, then glue descended quasi-affine pieces. Source locator: BLR 6.1/7 proof sketch read; the explicit affine-locus and descent proof follows below. For a qcqs scheme and a section s of a line bundle L, sections over Xs are localized sections: Gamma(Xs,F) is the colimit of Gamma(X,F tensor L to the n) under multiplication by s. Prove this on a finite trivializing affine cover: fractions represent sections locally, finitely many denominators clear, and finitely many overlap equalities clear after raising the power once more. This is an actual finite equalizer argument. In particular sections defining principal opens in a quasi-affine Xs extend after multiplying by a power of s. Multiplying once more by s makes their nonvanishing loci stay inside Xs. Choose principal affine opens of its affine ambient scheme containing each point. Their pulled-back functions give sections of powers of L with affine nonvanishing loci. Thus a finite cover by quasi-affine section loci implies the repository's affine-locus ampleness definition.

Conversely, if L is ample, every positive-power section s has quasi-affine nonvanishing locus. Choose a finite affine section-locus cover Xtj of X and raise powers so the degrees of tj and s agree. On Xs the functions tj/s define affine principal opens: their nonvanishing loci are Xtj intersect Xs, principal opens in affine Xtj. These cover Xs. The canonical map Xs to Spec Gamma(Xs,O) is an open immersion because localization of global sections identifies each such principal open with the corresponding distinguished open in that spectrum. This proves quasi-affineness.

For a fixed line bundle on a Noetherian separated finite-type R-scheme X and any faithfully flat DVR extension R to B, finite affine-cover equalizers give Gamma(X,F) tensor B=Gamma(XB,FB) for every quasi-coherent F, using flatness. If LB is ample, apply published `thm-serre-criterion-ampleness` to each coherent FB. The evaluation map for F tensor L to the n becomes surjective for all sufficiently large n after tensoring B. Its cokernel therefore vanishes by `thm-faithfully-flat-descent-vanishing`. Serre's criterion on X gives ampleness of L. This is the full DVR extension argument; the field-only published ampleness lemma is not silently widened.

 For quasi-projectivity of a finite-type separated R-scheme X with an ample line bundle L, choose finitely many affine section opens X_si covering X and raise the sections to a common positive degree. Each Γ(X_si,O) is a finite-type R-algebra; choose finitely many R-algebra generators f_ij. The section-extension lemma extends each f_ij si^n to a global section of L to a sufficiently large common power. After multiplication by further si powers, their ratios to si^n are exactly f_ij on X_si. Include each si^n in the finite global section list; they have no common zero and define a map X→P_R^M. On the projective chart for si^n its preimage is X_si, and the coordinate-ring map is surjective because its ratios include all f_ij. Thus the map is a closed immersion into the union of these projective charts, by closed-immersion locality on the target. That union is open in projective space, so the map to projective space is a locally closed immersion. This proof uses no properness of X.

references.title: Bosch, Lutkebohmert, Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 6.1/7 and 6.4/2-3 (divisor ampleness and quasi-projectivity)

items.title: Picard representation by generic quotient and translates
items.statement:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied scheme and cohomology results. Over an algebraically closed field, the full rigidified relative Picard functor of an abelian variety is represented by a separated locally finite-type group scheme, with a universal rigidified line bundle. Representation is on every test scheme, including nonreduced tests. Complete proof strategy: The image V of W in the Picard sheaf is an **open subfunctor**, not just a subset of geometric classes. For any T→Pic, first restrict to the open T+ where its line bundle has the fixed polynomial and finite positive-regularity conditions of the chosen chart. Polynomial local constancy and the finite-complex vanishing conditions make T+ open; finite-presentation descent treats arbitrary tests. Over T+ the divisor map is the faithfully flat open projective-space bundle of sections. Saturation makes the preimage of W invariant under its kernel pair, so that open descends to an open subset of T+, and therefore of T. On that descended open the pullback is represented by the quotient Y×_Pic T. The fppf sheaf quotient equality identifies V with Y. This proves an open immersion of represented functors V→Pic.

Translate V by every rigidified class over the algebraically closed base field k. These translates contain every k-valued class: choose v∈V(k), which exists since V is nonempty and locally of finite type, and for x∈Pic(k) use translation by x−v. To prove coverage on arbitrary tests, pull their union back to each finite-type positive divisor chart D for every polynomial and every sufficiently high twist. This pullback is open and contains every closed point of D, since closed points have residue field k. Its closed complement is therefore empty by the Nullstellensatz. The positive divisor charts, with twists reversed, cover the Picard sheaf fppf-locally on every test: locally a sufficiently positive twist has locally free nonzero sections and a fibrewise nonzero section exists after the projective-space cover. Hence every test pulls back to the union of the translates. Their represented open overlaps and identity transition maps glue to a scheme representing the full functor on all tests, including nonreduced and non-Noetherian tests. This chart argument does not assume that every geometric class descends to k.

 Apply the published generic quotient to the flat finite-type represented linear-equivalence relation from the preceding divisor chart, obtaining its saturated quotientable open W. The quotient Y is exactly the open subfunctor V, by descent through the relatively projective-space covering. Gluing all translated open subfunctors gives the whole representing sheaf, rather than a geometric-point bijection.

references.title: B. Edixhoven, G. van der Geer, B. Moonen, Abelian Varieties (2012), Chapters 6-9; local closure in owner-arithmetic-models/dual-source/proof-closure-packet.md

items.title: Good reduction supplies a Neron model
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Let $S$ be a Dedekind scheme with function field $K$ and let $A_K$ be an abelian variety over $K$ with good reduction over $S$. Then $A_K$ admits a Neron model over $S$, namely any abelian scheme model $A\to S$ of $A_K$, and this model is unique up to a unique $S$-isomorphism. In particular, for a discrete valuation ring $R$ with fraction field $K$, every abelian variety over $K$ with good reduction has a Neron model over $R$, and the Neron model in this class is proper and smooth over $R$.

references.title: S. Bosch, W. Lutkebohmert, M. Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 1.2/8 and 1.3/1 (good reduction and Neron models)

items.title: Good reduction is stable under base change of the base
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Let $S$ be a Dedekind scheme with function field $K$, let $A_K$ be an abelian variety with good reduction over $S$ witnessed by an abelian scheme $A\to S$, and let $S'\to S$ be a dominant morphism of Dedekind schemes with function field $K'$ (for instance the normalization of $S$ in a finite extension $K'/K$, or the localisation of $S$ at a point). Then $A_{S'}\to S'$ is an abelian scheme and $A_{K'}=A_{S'}\times_{S'}\operatorname{Spec}K'$ has good reduction over $S'$; the model $A_{S'}$ is the base change of the model $A$. In particular good reduction is preserved by finite extensions of the function field and by localisation of the base. Nothing is asserted here about the converse direction; the example and counterexample items on the companion page record the failure of descent along ramified base change. In addition, every abelian variety over a number field K has good reduction at all but finitely many finite places. For this spreading clause write K as the filtered colimit of O_K[1/d] for nonzero integers d. The finite-presentation scheme-stage and proper-stage suppliers descend A_K to a proper finitely presented model over one such ring. Descend multiplication, unit and inverse and their finitely many identities at a common later stage. The smooth locus is open; the closed nonsmooth locus has closed image by properness and misses the generic point, so inverting one further integer removes it. Smoothness gives base-flat O_A. Choose its universal finite projective cohomology complex. Over K, split its differentials and identify it with its finite-dimensional cohomology plus contractible pairs; all bases, inverse matrices and chain identities involve finitely many denominators and spread after inverting one further integer. The degree-zero remaining module has rank one because H0(A_K,O)=K. Therefore every geometric fibre has H0 of dimension one by universal cohomology comparison, and is connected: a disconnected proper fibre would give independent nontrivial clopen idempotents. Smoothness gives relative dimension g after discarding any components absent generically (their closed proper images miss the generic point). The resulting smooth proper finitely presented group with geometrically connected fibres is an abelian scheme. The removed closed set of Spec O_K is finite; localization at every remaining place proves the clause. This supplies the originally inline Lombardo4.10 harvest, rather than using base-change stability as a substitute for spreading.

references.title: S. Bosch, W. Lutkebohmert, M. Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 1.3 and Chapter 7 (base change of good reduction; spreading over number fields)

items.title: Connected smooth quasiprojective model proper special fibre
items.statement:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the stated suppliers. let R be a DVR and G/R a smooth separated finite-type quasi-projective scheme with generic fibre an abelian variety. If the special fibre is proper and geometrically connected, G is proper over R. Applied to the connected identity model, it becomes an abelian scheme. Proof strategy: Statement: let R be a DVR and G/R a smooth separated finite-type quasi-projective scheme with generic fibre an abelian variety. If the special fibre is proper and geometrically connected, G is proper over R. Applied to the connected identity model, it becomes an abelian scheme.

Selected complete proof using published coherent perfect-complex result, not full formal GAGA: properness descends under R→Rhat by thm-properness-descent-fpqc and completion faithful flatness. Over complete R embed G as an open subscheme of its projective schematic closure X in P^m_R (a locally closed immersion makes it open in its closure). Closure is t-torsion-free on coordinate charts because its ideal is contracted from the generic fibre, so X is R-flat. The proper generic fibre G_K is closed in projective space; hence X_K=G_K. The finite R-module H0(X,O_X) injects into H0(X_K,O)=K by flatness. Every member is integral over R, and R is integrally closed; the scalar inclusion gives H0(X,O)=R.

If X_k were disconnected, its nontrivial clopen partition defines compatible idempotents e_n in H0(X_n,O), X_n=X×R R/t^(n+1), since these nilpotent thickenings all have the same underlying topological space and the unique functions 0/1 on that partition glue. Invoke the EXACT Statement of lem-proper-flat-fp-cohomology-perfect-complex for the already projective flat X and O_X: its bounded finite projective complex C is concentrated in degrees ≥0, and naturally H0(X_n,O)=ker(C0/t^(n+1)→C1/t^(n+1)). Finite projective modules over complete R are complete, and inverse limits preserve kernels. Thus lim H0(X_n,O)=ker(C0→C1)=H0(X,O)=R. The compatible e_n would give a nontrivial idempotent in R, impossible. Hence X_k is connected. The open immersion G_k→X_k is also proper because its source is proper and target separated, so its image is closed and open, nonempty, and therefore all X_k. It is an isomorphism. Generic fibres already coincide; the complement X\G is empty, so G=X. Descend properness to R.

Exact required earlier statements: quasi-projective Neron identity model from the Neron branch's BLR6.4 packet; lem-proper-flat-fp-cohomology-perfect-complex; thm-properness-descent-fpqc; thm-flatness-of-noetherian-completion; lem-projective-coherent-cohomology-finite-and-vanishing; thm-global-functions-proper-integral-variety; thm-over-a-pid-flat-is-equivalent-to-torsion-free and cor-dvr-is-a-pid; lem-schematic-closure-and-dense-agreement for contracted generic-fibre schematic closure. The closure argument uses that smooth G is flat, hence schematically dense in its generic fibre closure; on each chart the contraction ideal satisfies t f in I implies f in I. The perfect-complex supplier assumes AC and DC: retain both. Its naturality in base algebras is essential to the compatible idempotent argument. This lemma does not claim that arbitrary smooth connected group models are quasi-projective.

Alternative full authoritative source: EGA IV3 15.7.10 gives separated finite-type universally submersive morphism with geometrically connected fibres and proper special fibre ⇒ proper near the special point. A group section supplies universal submersiveness. EGA III1 5.5.2 gives the complete-local proper clopen piece; connected generic fibre and the section force its complement empty. BUT this alternative uses proper-support formal GAGA III1 5.1.4 via5.1.8. It is not presently a standalone closed local proof. Retain downloaded evidence; do not invoke5.5.2 as an unexplained citation. The selected projective-closure proof avoids this bottleneck.

references.title: Bosch, Lutkebohmert, Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 6.5 and EGA IV3 15.7.10 (properness from the special fibre); local proof in owner-arithmetic-models/neron-source/closure-supplement.md

items.title: Abelian scheme torsion specialization unramified
items.statement:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the stated suppliers. for an abelian scheme A/R of relative dimension g, ell≠char k and every v, A[ell^v] is finite étale of rank ell^(2gv). Over Rsh, specialization identifies its generic geometric points with special separable points, and inertia acts trivially. Proof strategy: Statement: for an abelian scheme A/R of relative dimension g, ell≠char k and every v, A[ell^v] is finite étale of rank ell^(2gv). Over Rsh, specialization identifies its generic geometric points with special separable points, and inertia acts trivially.

Proof: helper2 gives étaleness of [ell^v]; properness of [ell^v] and finite geometric fibres from field multiplication make it finite (thm-proper-quasi-finite-is-finite). Its kernel is finite étale. The rank is locally constant and equals ell^(2gv) on the generic fibre by helper3, hence everywhere on connected SpecR. Helper1 decomposes it over Rsh as copies of SpecRsh, so its geometric generic points are already rational over Ksh and specialization is a bijection. Its Galois action therefore factors through the residue Galois action, and inertia is trivial. This is the precise finite-étale smooth-proper specialization claimed here; it is not general smooth proper base change for H^i.

references.title: S. Bosch, W. Lutkebohmert, M. Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 7.3/2 and 7.4 (torsion of abelian schemes and inertia)

items.title: Birational group law
items.statement: Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied algebra and scheme results. Let R be a DVR, K its fraction field, k its residue field, and Rsh a chosen strict henselization. In clauses involving A, let A/K be the given abelian variety. The generic multiplication of A extends to an R-birational associative law on X with both universal translations birational. Complete proof strategy: At each special generic point of the first X factor, apply P10 to the universal generic translation over its local DVR; spread to an R-rational universal left translation. Repeat for the right translation. Their multiplication projections agree generically, and associativity follows by separated dense agreement. Source locators: BLR 4.3/5.  An R-birational group law means an R-rational multiplication m on X×_R X which is associative wherever the compositions are defined and whose universal left and right translations (x,y)↦(x,m(x,y)) and (x,y)↦(m(x,y),y) are R-birational self-maps of X×_R X. An R-birational map has an inverse represented on fibre-dense opens.

references.title: Bosch, Lutkebohmert, Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 4.3/5 (birational group law from the minimal model)

items.title: Coherent Kunneth, the tangent bound and the proper-image dual
items.statement:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied scheme and cohomology results. For an abelian variety A of dimension g over an algebraically closed field, H^1(A,O_A) has dimension at most g, the Picard tangent space at zero is H^1(A,O_A), and the Picard zero component is a smooth proper connected group B of dimension g. Every ample L gives an isogeny phi_L:A→B with finite kernel. Complete proof strategy: 

For coherent cohomology over a field, use the double Čech complex for the two finite separated affine covers. On each product of affine intersections its sections are the tensor product of the two section modules. The two augmented Čech directions compute cohomology because affine quasi-coherent higher cohomology vanishes; thus its total complex computes the product cohomology. Applying field Künneth to that tensor total complex gives the cohomology tensor product, with Koszul signs. Thus H^*(A,O_A) is a connected graded Hopf algebra via addition. Every element of H1 is primitive. If v1,…,vr are independent in H1, apply the r-fold coproduct to v1⋯vr and project to (H1)^⊗r. The result is the signed sum over permutations of the distinct tensors v_(σ1)⊗⋯⊗v_(σr). These tensors are independent; each coefficient is ±1, so the result is nonzero even in characteristic 2. Therefore H^r≠0 and r≤g. **No Borel structure theorem is needed for this bound.**

The exact sequence 1→1+εO_A→O^*_(A[ε])→O_A^*→1 identifies the rigidified Picard tangent space with H1(A,O_A). It follows that tangent dimension≤g. For ample L, the published cube/square and the local ample-kernel argument supplied below defines φ_L into Pic with finite scheme kernel, hence image dimension g. Since Pic is separated, the morphism from proper A is proper. Its image is closed, connected, and has dimension g. At the identity, local dimension g and embedding dimension≤g force a regular local ring; translation makes the whole identity neighbourhood smooth. The proper image contains an open neighbourhood of the identity, and translations give open image everywhere. It is open and closed and therefore equals Pic0. Hence B=Pic0 is a smooth proper finite-type connected group of dimension g, and φ_L:A→B is an isogeny. This avoids assuming projective Picard components or separately invoking a compactness theorem for the identity component.

For ample L, K=ker(phi_L) is represented by the just constructed Picard scheme. The normalized family Lambda(L) is trivial on A×K by the full kernel universal property. Over an algebraic closure Y=K^0_red is a smooth connected proper subgroup, hence an abelian subvariety: reduced finite-type groups over a perfect field are smooth by translation of the nonempty smooth locus. Restrict Lambda(L) to Y×Y and pull it back by (id,-id). This makes L|Y⊗[-1]^*L|Y trivial. It is ample, since L|Y is ample, inverse is an automorphism and tensor products of ample sheaves are ample. A trivial ample line bundle on a proper integral variety forces dimension zero: a high power embeds it, but all sections of the trivial bundle are scalars, so the embedding is constant. Thus dimY=0, K is zero-dimensional proper finite type, and therefore finite, including its nonreduced structure. This is EGM2.17–2.19, whose proof was read; no pre-existing ample-kernel theorem is presumed. Invariant differentials trivialize Omega_A: universal translation carries the cotangent space at e to every point, and the inverse translation gives the inverse bundle map. Thus wedge^g Omega_A is trivial. In the proper-image argument local dimension equals tangent dimension g at every translated point, giving smoothness over the algebraically closed field. The image is both open and closed, hence exactly the connected zero component.

references.title: B. Edixhoven, G. van der Geer, B. Moonen, Abelian Varieties (2012), 2.17-2.19 and Chapter 6 (Picard tangent and ampleness); closure in owner-arithmetic-models/dual-source/proof-closure-packet.md

items.title: Strictification
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Let X be a smooth separated faithfully flat finite-type model over a DVR R with an R-birational group law and birational universal translations. There exists an R-dense model open Xzero inside X carrying a strict birational group law, with multiplication domain Uzero inside Xzero times Xzero and universal translations open immersions whose domains and images are dense over both projections. Xzero remains smooth separated faithfully flat finite type. In the commissioned abelian minimal-model case, the generic law is everywhere defined, so Xzero_K=X_K=A. Complete proof: form a common R-dense domain U of the universal translations and images V,W, and set Z=U intersect V intersect W. Its two bad-density loci in X are constructible and omit every fibre generic point. Separate their generic and special parts: the schematic closure of the generic part has a uniformizer-saturated ideal, which cannot be nonzero proper in a special height-one DVR local ring; the special constructible part has nondense closure by the dense-constructible-open lemma. Removing both closures gives the model open Xzero. Define Uzero=U intersect Xzero squared intersect m inverse Xzero. The original translation open immersions give density of its domain in each projection; for the remaining image densities, fix a output point a and use the two open immersions of m inverse(a) onto dense opens of X times a and a times X. This yields full both-projection density and cancellation on arbitrary tests by universal schematic density. This restores BLR 5.2/2, not a claim that arbitrary constructible closures over a DVR contain every special generic point they meet.

references.title: Bosch, Lutkebohmert, Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 5.2/2 and 2.5/1 (strictification of a birational group law)

items.title: Finite-field descent of the dual and the Poincare bundle
items.statement: Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied scheme and cohomology results. Let $A$ be an abelian variety over a field $k$. Then the algebraically trivial rigidified Picard subfunctor of $A/k$ is represented by an abelian variety $A^\vee$ of dimension $\dim A$, together with a normalized Poincare bundle $\mathcal P$ on $A\times_kA^\vee$, and the formation and full universal property are compatible with field extension.

references.title: B. Edixhoven, G. van der Geer, B. Moonen, Abelian Varieties (2012), Chapters 8-9 (dual abelian variety and Poincare bundle)

items.title: Strict law graph calculus
items.statement: Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied algebra and scheme results. Let R be a DVR, K its fraction field, k its residue field, and Rsh a chosen strict henselization. In clauses involving A, let A/K be the given abelian variety. For a strict law, X embeds into the functor of relative birational self-maps. The closure of its multiplication graph has all three two-coordinate projections open immersions with both-projection dense images. Section translation is defined at b iff the law is defined at (a,b). Complete proof strategy: Injectivity follows from universal-right-translation cancellation; associativity identifies translation products. Test graph-closure triples on a dense extra variable w to prove ta tb=tc. Any two coordinates then determine the third even on T-valued points; quasi-finite birational graph projections are open by F04. Close each section-translation graph to obtain the final domain claim. Source locators: BLR 5.2/4; 5.3/1–4.

references.title: Bosch, Lutkebohmert, Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 5.2/4 and 5.3/1-4 (graph calculus of a strict law)

items.title: Homogeneous bundles and Mumford surjectivity
items.statement:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied scheme and cohomology results. For every abelian variety A/k a line bundle M has phi_M=0 exactly when its class belongs to Pic^0; if M is nontrivial and homogeneous then every H^i(A,M) vanishes. Over an algebraic closure every homogeneous M is t_x^*L⊗L^{-1} for some x, for any fixed ample L. The equality ker(phi)=Pic^0 holds as a sheaf on all tests. Complete proof strategy: 

For a bundle M with φ_M=0, the square/cube plus rigidification gives m^*M=p1^*M⊗p2^*M. If H0(M)≠0, also H0(M^−1)≠0 by inversion; their product is a nonzero constant, forcing M trivial. If i is the least index of nonzero cohomology of a nontrivial M, pullback by m followed by restriction along (id,0) is the identity on H^i(M). Künneth says the intermediate cohomology is ⊕_(a+b=i)H^a(M)⊗H^b(M), zero by minimality and H0=0. This contradiction proves H^i(M)=0 for all i.

For fixed ample L, if no x satisfies M=t_x^*L⊗L^−1, set Q=Λ(L)⊗p2^*M^−1. Horizontal fibres are nontrivial homogeneous bundles, so Rp1_*Q=0 by the universal cohomology complex. Vertical fibres are homogeneous and vanish except over finite K(L); thus every R^ip2_*Q has finite support. Leray gives H^*(Q)=0 via p1 and then R^ip2_*Q=0 via p2, contradicting the trivial vertical fibre at zero and derived base change. Therefore φ_L exhausts the homogeneous geometric classes. Since the Picard scheme is smooth and φ is constant on connected families by rigidity, ker φ=Pic0 as a sheaf, not only on points. Write this family argument against the universal bundle and then pull back to arbitrary tests.

 For the all-test kernel identification apply proper-factor rigidity to the morphism A×B→A^vee induced by the universal Poincare bundle: at the zero parameter it is zero, so it is identically zero. On every translate of B the universal Mumford morphism is therefore constant. A nonzero constant morphism cannot become zero after a nonempty scalar extension. This establishes the kernel subfunctor scheme-theoretically, including infinitesimal tests.

references.title: B. Edixhoven, G. van der Geer, B. Moonen, Abelian Varieties (2012), Chapter 8 (homogeneous bundles and Mumford surjectivity)

items.title: Separated translate gluing
items.statement: Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied algebra and scheme results. Let R be a DVR, K its fraction field, k its residue field, and Rsh a chosen strict henselization. In clauses involving A, let A/K be the given abelian variety. Over a normal strictly henselian local base, gluing X to a left translate X(a) along the closed section-translation graph gives a smooth separated finite-type scheme and extends the strict law. Complete proof strategy: Both graph projections are open immersions and closed graph gives separated gluing. Define the law on X times X, X(a) times X, and X times X(a) using associativity; verify both universal translations are open by graph calculus and their images dense. Source locators: BLR 5.3/5.

references.title: Bosch, Lutkebohmert, Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 5.3/5 (gluing a translate)

items.title: Dual isogeny kernels and canonical biduality
items.statement:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied scheme and cohomology results. Every isogeny f:A→C (a surjective homomorphism with finite scheme-theoretic kernel) has dual isogeny f^vee:C^vee→A^vee whose kernel is (kerf)^D as a group scheme and whose degree equals degf. The canonical Poincare morphism kappa:A→A^{vee vee} is an isomorphism; dual pullback is contravariantly functorial on homomorphisms and additive for parallel homomorphisms f,g:A→C. Complete proof strategy: For an isogeny f:A→C with kernel H, f is the fppf quotient. A rigidified bundle M on C_T with f^*M trivial descends the trivial bundle on A_T with H_T-action. Universal constants force any such action to be a character H_T→Gm,T. Trivializations differ only by a base unit, so the character is independent of choice; conversely character descent produces M. Tensor and base change commute with the construction. All these bundles are in Pic0: the character is killed by d=rank H, so its d-th tensor descent datum is trivial and M^d is rigidified-trivial. Hence d·φ_M=0. The pointed morphism φ_M into finite affine C^vee[d]_T factors through T by universal structure sections, and its factor is zero; thus φ_M=0 on every test. Hence ker f^∨=H^D **as group schemes**, with no reduced-kernel restriction. Finite rank equality gives deg f^∨=deg f; dimension and finite kernel give an isogeny.

Switching the normalized Poincaré bundle defines κ_A:A→B^∨. Symmetry of Λ(L) gives φ_L=φ_L^∨κ_A on every test. Its finite kernel makes κ_A an isogeny. Degree equality for φ_L and its dual then gives deg κ_A=1, so κ_A is an isomorphism. Pullback of normalized bundles gives contravariance and composition; the cube identity gives (f+g)^vee=f^vee+g^vee for homomorphisms f,g:A→C with a common source and target.



The Poincare pullback (id_A times phi_L)^*P_A is on A times A. Comparing the defining dual pullback with the switched Poincare bundle gives phi_L=phi_L^vee composed with kappa_A using the symmetry of the normalized square family; no ill-typed A times A^vee pullback is used. Projectivity supplies the ample L.

references.title: B. Edixhoven, G. van der Geer, B. Moonen, Abelian Varieties (2012), 6.13-6.20 (dual abelian variety)
S. Bosch, W. Lutkebohmert, M. Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 8.1 (rigidified line bundles and the dual abelian variety)

items.title: Theta extensions, splitting and isotropic descent
items.statement:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied scheme and cohomology results. For a line bundle N on A and a finite subgroup H⊂K(N), the theta group over H is a G_m-extension with an alternating bilinear commutator. If the commutator is trivial on H over an algebraically closed field, the extension splits, giving H-linearization and descent of N through A→A/H. Complete proof strategy: 

For λ:A→B, set M=(id,λ)^*P. Biextension identities give φ_M=λ+λ^∨. If λ is symmetric, N=M² has φ_N=4λ. Thus A[4]⊂K(N). The theta commutator e_N on A[4] has values in μ4, and e_N(2y,2z)=e_N(y,z)^4=1. Since [2]:A[4]→A[2] is fppf onto, A[2] is isotropic scheme theoretically even in characteristic 2.

Here is a local replacement for EGM's deferred Ext(H,Gm)=0 fact, once finite Cartier exactness is proved. Let 0→Gm→E→H→0 be a commutative extension over an algebraically closed field and n annihilate H. Then [n]:E→Gm restricts to the nth-power map on Gm, and F=E[n]→H is a finite μn-torsor. Cartier exactness makes F^D→(μn)^D=Z/n fppf onto. A nonempty finite scheme over an algebraically closed field has a rational point, so choose χ:F→Gm restricting to the tautological μn character. The map Gm×F→E, (t,h)↦th, is a μn-torsor; (t,h)↦tχ(h) is invariant under its kernel and descends to a retraction E→Gm. Its kernel maps isomorphically to H, so the extension splits. Applying this to the theta extension over an isotropic subgroup supplies a linearization, and ordinary flat descent gives N=[2]^*L. Then 4λ=4φ_L and cancellation through the fppf epimorphism [4] gives λ=φ_L.

 The theta extension is represented by the invertible scalar-isomorphism torsor of the normalized trivial family on A×K(N). Compose the translation isomorphisms to obtain multiplication; central scalar automorphisms give the G_m kernel. The commutator is central, alternating and bilinear by the group commutator identities. Scheme-theoretic isotropy, the finite Cartier-dual splitting argument and module descent apply to all tests, not only geometric points.

references.title: B. Edixhoven, G. van der Geer, B. Moonen, Abelian Varieties (2012), 8.1-8.11 (theta groups, extensions by Gm and descent of line bundles)
S. Bosch, W. Lutkebohmert, M. Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 8.1 (rigidified Picard functor and Poincare bundle)

items.title: Poincare cohomology at the identity
items.statement:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied scheme and cohomology results. For the normalized Poincare bundle P on A×A^vee, with dimA=g, Rp_{2*}P is concentrated in degree g, where R^gp_{2*}P is the length-one skyscraper at zero. In particular the conclusion retains infinitesimal scheme lengths. Complete proof strategy: 

For P on A×B, nontrivial homogeneous fibre bundles have no cohomology. Thus all R^ip2_*P are supported at zero. At R=O_(B,0), take a finite free universal cohomology complex K in degrees 0,…,g: fibre cohomology vanishes outside that interval, so split off the acyclic tails using invertible differential minors and Nakayama. All its cohomology modules have finite length because their support is the closed point. The shifted dual C=Hom_R(K,R)[−g] (so C^i=Hom_R(K^{g−i},R), with the usual dual signs) is also concentrated in 0,…,g and has finite-length cohomology: away from the closed point K is a split exact complex of finite free modules, and so is C. Apply the following local acyclicity argument to K and to C, obtaining vanishing below degree g for both. This supplies the concentration argument directly, without an unsupported global Leray/duality inference. For completeness, a bounded nonnegative free complex C over a g-dimensional regular local ring R, all of whose cohomology has finite length, has H^i(C)=0 for i<g. Choose a regular parameter system x1,…,xg. Let E be the augmented localization Čech complex R→⊕R[xi^−1]→⋯→R[(x1⋯xg)^−1] in degrees 0,…,g. The complex E is the filtered direct limit of cohomologically oriented Koszul complexes on x1^n,…,xg^n; each power sequence is regular, so E has no cohomology below g. This uses exactness of filtered colimits of modules and the ordinary Koszul regular-sequence theorem. Apply the two spectral sequences of the bounded double complex C⊗E. Computing E first yields no total cohomology in degrees below g since C starts in degree zero. Computing C first, flatness of each localization gives H^i(C) tensored with E. Every finite-length R-module is killed by a power of the maximal ideal, so all its nonempty parameter localizations are zero; its E-cohomology is itself in degree zero. This second spectral sequence degenerates and identifies total cohomology in degree i with H^i(C). Therefore H^i(C)=0 for i<g. Apply this to the dual cohomology complex. This explicit proof avoids incorrectly applying a length-g induction hypothesis to a length-g complex over dimension g−1.

Split off any remaining differential unit entries to choose a minimal finite free complex over R. Its differential vanishes after reduction to k, so dim H0(A,O)=dim Hg(A,O)=1 makes K0 and Kg rank one; the latter equality uses Serre duality and the trivial canonical bundle. Hence both terminal cokernels, for K and C, are cyclic. Write the dual terminal cokernel R/J. Its dual description of H0 after reduction shows that the section 1 on the zero fibre lifts over Spec R/J; Nakayama makes the induced section of P invertible there. The **full** universal property forces Spec R/J→B to factor through zero, so J is the maximal ideal. The dual complex is therefore a free resolution of k. Compare it by chain lifting with the Koszul resolution on a regular parameter system; resolutions by projectives are homotopy equivalent. Dualizing back yields terminal cokernel k. Hence Rp2_*P=k(0)[−g]. This is EGM's second proof, with its unproved references replaced by ordinary complex, regular-local and Koszul suppliers; it needs neither the Borel theorem nor general relative Grothendieck duality.

references.title: B. Edixhoven, G. van der Geer, B. Moonen, Abelian Varieties (2012), 9.1-9.6 (cohomology of the Poincare bundle)
D. Mumford, Abelian Varieties (1970), III.13 and the Fourier-Mukai computation of Rp_2(P)

items.title: Finite translate completion and uniqueness
items.statement: Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied algebra and scheme results. Let R be a DVR, K its fraction field, k its residue field, and Rsh a chosen strict henselization. In clauses involving A, let A/K be the given abelian variety. For a strict law on a smooth separated faithfully flat finite-type model X over a strictly henselian DVR, finitely many section translates yield Y on which original X times X multiplication is everywhere defined. Y becomes a smooth separated finite-type group scheme containing X as fibre-dense open; any two group completions of a birational law are canonically isomorphic. Complete proof strategy: The multiplication graph domains Qn form increasing opens of the fixed Noetherian X times X, so stabilize. If a section translation still fails, glue its translate and strictly increase Qn, contradiction. Sections meet all dense opens in either fibre: for the generic fibre, specialize its excluded closed set and use dimension/flatness to leave a dense special open. Factor multiplication near any pair through a suitable such section. Source locators: BLR 5.3/6–7 specialized to DVR; BLR 5.3/8; 5.1/3–4. For generic auxiliary a express bc=(ba)(a inverse c); strict graph calculus puts the two factors in original X on a dense faithfully flat cover, and global X times X multiplication makes the law defined there. Descend its domain. Repeat for left division; the representable subgroup of birational maps supplies unit and inverse. Uniqueness uses the smooth surjection X times X to each completion and morphism descent. Source locators: BLR 5.3/6–7 specialized to DVR; BLR 5.3/8; 5.1/3–4.

items.title: Symmetric homomorphisms are Mumford maps
items.statement:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied scheme and cohomology results. For any field k and any symmetric lambda:A→A^vee, there is a finite separable extension k'/k and a line bundle L on A_{k'} with lambda_{k'}=phi_L. In particular this holds over every separably closed field, including characteristic two. Complete proof strategy: 

For λ:A→B, set M=(id,λ)^*P. Biextension identities give φ_M=λ+λ^∨. If λ is symmetric, N=M² has φ_N=4λ. Thus A[4]⊂K(N). The theta commutator e_N on A[4] has values in μ4, and e_N(2y,2z)=e_N(y,z)^4=1. Since [2]:A[4]→A[2] is fppf onto, A[2] is isotropic scheme theoretically even in characteristic 2.

Here is a local replacement for EGM's deferred Ext(H,Gm)=0 fact, once finite Cartier exactness is proved. Let 0→Gm→E→H→0 be a commutative extension over an algebraically closed field and n annihilate H. Then [n]:E→Gm restricts to the nth-power map on Gm, and F=E[n]→H is a finite μn-torsor. Cartier exactness makes F^D→(μn)^D=Z/n fppf onto. A nonempty finite scheme over an algebraically closed field has a rational point, so choose χ:F→Gm restricting to the tautological μn character. The map Gm×F→E, (t,h)↦th, is a μn-torsor; (t,h)↦tχ(h) is invariant under its kernel and descends to a retraction E→Gm. Its kernel maps isomorphically to H, so the extension splits. Applying this to the theta extension over an isotropic subgroup supplies a linearization, and ordinary flat descent gives N=[2]^*L. Then 4λ=4φ_L and cancellation through the fppf epimorphism [4] gives λ=φ_L.

 To represent the realizing-bundle torsor over k, spread the realizing line bundle and equality from the algebraic closure to a finite field extension K/k. Over K it is represented by A^vee_K using the Poincare bundle and all-test kernel equality. The canonical finite-field descent datum is effective because this projective representative has affine-contained finite descent orbits; Serre vanishing supplies the required affine opens. The descended torsor is nonempty smooth finite type, so a finite separable point realizes lambda. This does not assume representability of the full Picard scheme over k.

references.title: B. Edixhoven, G. van der Geer, B. Moonen, Abelian Varieties (2012), 11.1-11.2 (symmetric homomorphisms are Mumford maps over a finite separable extension)

items.title: The square degree of a Mumford map
items.statement:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied scheme and cohomology results. Let $A$ be an abelian variety of dimension $g$ over a field $k$ and let $\mathcal L$ be a nondegenerate invertible sheaf on $A$, that is, $K(\mathcal L)=\ker\varphi_{\mathcal L}$ is finite. Then
$$\deg\varphi_{\mathcal L}=\chi(A,\mathcal L)^2,$$
where $\deg\varphi_{\mathcal L}$ is the finite locally free rank of the isogeny $\varphi_{\mathcal L}$; the identity retains characteristic-dividing degrees and the full nonreduced scheme length of $K(\mathcal L)$. Consequently the degree of every polarization of $A$ ([[def-polarization-of-an-abelian-variety]]) is a perfect square.

items.title: Effective ample pair and group descent
items.statement:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied algebra and scheme results. Let R be a DVR, K its fraction field, k its residue field, and Rsh a chosen strict henselization. In clauses involving A, let A/K be the given abelian variety. If the smooth separated finite-type group completion H/Rsh with abelian generic fibre of the strict law on U_Rsh has a stable fibre-dense open U with effective descent to R, its compatible group descent datum is effective. The canonical datum on U_Rsh extends uniquely to a group datum on H and satisfies the triple cocycle; U stays stable and effectively descends. Schemes form an fpqc stack for morphisms, quasi-affine schemes have effective descent, and smoothness, finite presentation, separatedness, and open immersions descend fpqc. Complete proof strategy: Choose a fibre-dense affine open in descended U by F10; pull it back. Choose a generic divisor with complementary support on known generic A, close it in H, and exclude vertical components by fibre-density to get support exactly H minus U. Flat closure preserves the divisor datum, so O(D) has a compatible linearization. P19 gives ampleness, and effective ample pair descent gives H/R and its group maps. Source locators: BLR 6.5/1 proof under condition (a); BLR 6.5/2. Over Rsh tensor R Rsh the two pulled-back completions solve the same strict law; use the uniqueness proof which holds over arbitrary base to extend the canonical U isomorphism. Triple uniqueness gives cocycle. This does not require the tensor-product ring to be a DVR. Source locators: BLR 6.5/1 proof under condition (a); BLR 6.5/2. Use the affine equalizer for morphisms; descend ambient global-section algebras for quasi-affine schemes and descend stable opens using quotient topology. Check finite presentations and geometric conditions locally. Source locator: BLR 6.1/4, /6 proofs read; modules/algebras supplier mapped; the exact property-descent argument follows below. For effective descent of an ample pair (Xprime,Lprime) from Rsh to R, form the graded global section algebra. Flat base change of its graded pieces and the pair cocycle give algebra descent; `lem-nonaffine-effective-affine-algebra-descent` supplies the actual invariant algebra A and identifies Rsh tensor A with the section algebra. Each section upstairs is a finite sum of scalar multiples of descended sections of the same degree. If that section generates Lprime at a point, at least one descended section does too. Every such nonvanishing open is quasi-affine by the preceding argument and stable under the datum. Quasi-affine descent is direct: embed that open in Spec of its global sections, descend the algebra, and take its image under the faithfully flat spectrum map. Stability makes the inverse image of that image exactly the original open; `lem-fpqc-cover-submersive` makes the image open. These descended opens glue because compatible morphisms descend by the same affine algebra equalizer. The invertible sheaf descends on the resulting scheme by module descent on each affine chart; rank-one freeness is checked faithfully flat, or via dual evaluation and finite-generator descent. This establishes effective ample-pair descent, including actual scheme representability.

For the descended group G, exact `lem-fpqc-descent-properness-components` supplies finite type and separatedness. Since R is Noetherian, finite type gives local finite presentation. Flatness descends by `thm-faithfully-flat-descent-of-flatness`. For each residue field, geometric regularity descends by `lem-ag-geometric-regularity-field-tests`. Thus the smoothness criterion supplies smooth G. Multiplication, inverse and unit descend as compatible morphisms; their identities hold after the faithfully flat base change, hence hold below. This proves every geometric-property use needed here.

An ample pair means a finite-type scheme Xprime with an ample invertible sheaf; Xprime need not be quasi-affine, while its nonvanishing section opens are quasi-affine. This restores the source-correct full ample-pair descent assertion. Group descent (b) uses abelian generic fibre because that is the complete cube/square/ampleness route supplied here. The commissioned completion case (c) has U_K=A and H_Ksh=A_Ksh, so its full canonical descent and Neron conclusions are preserved. Broader arbitrary-group descent is true in BLR via a general positive-power square theorem, but that broader foundation is not admitted as a local proof supplier.

references.title: S. Bosch, W. Lutkebohmert, M. Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 6.1/4, 6.1/6 and 6.5/1-6.5/2 (effective descent and group completions)

items.title: The dual abelian variety, the Poincare bundle and polarizations
items.statement: Assume AC and DC as inherited from projectivity and the supplied cohomology machinery. Let $A$ be an abelian variety over a field $k$, of dimension $g$. Then: (a) [existence and duality] the degree-zero part of the rigidified relative Picard functor of $A/k$ is representable by an abelian variety $\hat A$, the dual abelian variety, of dimension $g$, with universal Poincare sheaf $\mathcal P$ on $A\times_k\hat A$; the canonical homomorphism $A\to\hat{\hat A}$ is an isomorphism; (b) [functoriality] $A\mapsto\hat A$ is a contravariant functor on abelian varieties over $k$, and for every isogeny $f:A\to B$ the dual $f^\vee:\hat B\to\hat A$ is an isogeny with kernel the Cartier dual of $\ker f$; (c) [Mumford maps] for every invertible sheaf $\mathcal L$ on $A$ the Mumford homomorphism $\varphi_{\mathcal L}:A\to\hat A$ exists; if $\mathcal L$ is ample then $\varphi_{\mathcal L}$ is an isogeny with finite kernel $K(\mathcal L)$, and every symmetric homomorphism $A\to\hat A$ is $\varphi_{\mathcal L}$ for some invertible sheaf $\mathcal L$ after base change to a separably closed field; (d) [polarizations] an ample $\mathcal L$ makes $\varphi_{\mathcal L}$ a polarization, every abelian variety admits a polarization, the degree of a polarization is a perfect square, and $A$ is projective. Complete locally supplied proof route: divisor Hilbert charts and the published generic flat-relation quotient construct representable open Picard subfunctors; translations glue the full all-test Picard functor. A primitive coherent H1 tangent bound plus the proper ample Mumford image constructs Pic0, and finite-field effective descent supplies the arbitrary-field dual and Poincare bundle. Character descent proves dual Cartier kernels and degree cancellation proves biduality. The finite theta extension splits by finite Cartier exactness, including characteristic two, giving symmetric-map realization over a finite separable extension. Poincare cohomology is proved using the nonnegative finite free complex and a Cech/Koszul finite-length argument; Euler characteristic gives degree chi(L)^2. Every source result consumed here is either an exact published interface or a local helper with the argument supplied; no Picard representability or Neron theorem is assumed by citation.

items.title: Full minimal model embedding
items.statement: Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied algebra and scheme results. Let R be a DVR, K its fraction field, k its residue field, and Rsh a chosen strict henselization. In clauses involving A, let A/K be the given abelian variety. The descended completion contains the full separated minimal model X supplied by lem-arith-separated-minimal-model-and-translations, not only the strictification U, as an R-dense open. Complete proof strategy: The rational X to G map is defined on U and entire generic A, hence in codimension one. P22 extends it. Its pulled-back invariant volume has no codimension-one zeros and hence no zeros; it is etale. Generic identity plus F04 makes it an open immersion. Source locators: BLR 5.1/5 final assertion.

items.title: Existence of Neron models for abelian varieties over a discrete valuation ring
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Let R be an arbitrary DVR, with fraction field K and residue field k, and let A_K be an abelian variety over K. There exists a smooth separated finite-type R-group scheme N with generic fibre A_K such that for every smooth R-scheme Z restriction Hom_R(Z,N)→Hom_K(Z_K,A_K) is bijective. N is unique up to unique isomorphism inducing the given generic-fibre identity. No excellence, completeness, perfect-residue-field or reduction-type hypothesis is imposed. Complete proof strategy: For irreducible special-fibre component of Z, at its generic point use P10 over the local DVR to extend universal translation by uK on Z times X. This is an R-rational map; generic definedness plus fibre-generic definedness covers all codimension-one points on the smooth source. View its second coordinate as an R-rational map Z times G to G. Its domain includes the whole generic fibre and all special-fibre generic points, so it includes every codimension-one point. Apply P22 over R to this smooth source and group target, then evaluate at the unit. Work locally on finite-type opens of Z and glue. Separatedness gives uniqueness. Combine projective weak model, minimal model, birational law, strict henselian translate completion, stable-open ample descent and Weil extension. No step assumes excellence, completeness, perfect residue field, dimension one for A, or reduction type. The locally ordered helper DAG supplies projective weak models, finite smoothening, invariant-volume minimal models, birational-law strictification, graph/translation completion over the strict henselization, an ample stable-open descent, full original-model embedding and regular-DVR Weil extension. The weak-model construction uses proper projective closure, so BLR general bounded-model or Artin-approximation branches are unnecessary. Relative rational maps are over R; the final universal-translation argument does not assert that an R-rational map is automatically Z-rational. On Z×_R N extend generic translation, apply the regular-base Weil theorem over R, then evaluate at the unit. All auxiliary field and scheme arguments are detailed in the exact current supplier packet and closure supplement.

references.title: S. Bosch, W. Lutkebohmert, M. Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), 1.3/1 and 4.4/4 (existence of Neron models and the mapping property)

items.title: Neron ogg shafarevich prime to residue characteristic
items.statement:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the stated suppliers. for an abelian variety A/K of dimension g with finite-type Neron model N/R and prime ell≠char k, the following are equivalent: good reduction by an abelian scheme; N is an abelian scheme; all A[ell^v](Ksep) are inertia-fixed; T_ell A is inertia-unramified. Proof strategy: Statement: for an abelian variety A/K of dimension g with finite-type Neron model N/R and prime ell≠char k, the following are equivalent: good reduction by an abelian scheme; N is an abelian scheme; all A[ell^v](Ksep) are inertia-fixed; T_ell A is inertia-unramified.

Proof: good reduction identifies the abelian scheme with the Neron model by the Neron branch's abelian-scheme mapping property and uniqueness; helper7 gives inertia invariance; helper3 gives equivalence finite torsion/Tate invariance. Conversely, Neron sections over Rsh are exactly A(Ksh), and helper2+1 identify N[ell^v](Rsh) with N_k[ell^v](ksep). Invariance means all ell^v-torsion is over Ksh, so helper3 gives cardinal ell^(2gv) on the special fibre for every v. Helper5 makes N_k^0 abelian. The Neron identity component N^0 is smooth separated finite type, its generic fibre is A, and its geometric special fibre is connected/proper. Neron-branch quasi-projectivity plus helper6 makes N^0 an abelian scheme. Its Neron property makes N=N^0 by uniqueness. Source BLR7.4/5; full local detail expanded above.

J.-P. Serre, J. Tate, Good reduction of abelian varieties, Ann. of Math. 88 (1968), Theorem 1

items.title: Good reduction, coherent base change, and unramified torsion
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Dependent Choice, inherited from the cohomology-and-base-change suppliers. Let $S$ be a Dedekind scheme with function field $K$, let $f:A\to S$ be an abelian scheme of relative dimension $g$, and let $A_K$ be its generic fibre. Then:

(a) [good reduction] $A_K$ is an abelian variety with good reduction over $S$, the abelian scheme model $A$ is unique up to a unique $S$-isomorphism inducing the specified identity on $A_K$, and $A$ is the Neron model of $A_K$; for every closed point $s\in S$ the fibre $A_s$ is an abelian variety of dimension $g$ over $\kappa(s)$.

(b) [base change] For every morphism $S'\to S$ the base change $A_{S'}\to S'$ is an abelian scheme of relative dimension $g$, it represents the base change of the good reduction data, and if $S'$ is a Dedekind scheme with function field $K'$ and $S'\to S$ is dominant so that $K\to K'$ is defined, then $A_{K'}$ has good reduction over $S'$.

(c) [coherent cohomology and base change] Fix $s\in S$, $q\ge0$ and a coherent $\mathcal O_A$-module $\mathcal F$ flat over $S$, and let $\varphi_s^q:(R^qf_*\mathcal F)(s)\to H^q(A_s,\mathcal F_s)$ be the cohomology-and-base-change map. If $\varphi_s^q$ is surjective, then there is an affine open neighbourhood $U\subseteq S$ of $s$ such that for every $T\to U$ the base-change map $h^*(R^qf_*\mathcal F|_U)\to R^qf'_{T*}(g_T^*\mathcal F)$ is an isomorphism; if moreover $\varphi_s^{q-1}$ is surjective, then $R^qf_*\mathcal F$ is finite locally free on a neighbourhood of $s$. For $q=0$ and $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_A$ the unit map $\mathcal O_S\to f_*\mathcal O_A$ is an isomorphism, with inverse evaluation along the identity section, and for $\mathcal F$ a line bundle flat over $S$ the higher direct images are finite locally free wherever the successive base-change maps are surjective.

(d) [residue restrictions] No restriction on the residue characteristic of $S$ is imposed in (a)-(c); the finite flatness conclusions in (c) are stated under the exact surjectivity hypotheses of the cohomology-and-base-change theorem, because fibrewise cohomology of smooth proper families need not be locally constant in residue characteristic $p>0$.

(e) [prime-to-residue-characteristic etale good reduction] Locally let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring, $K$ its fraction field and $k$ its residue field, $A_K$ an abelian variety and $\ell$ a prime different from $\operatorname{char}k$. Then $A_K$ has good reduction over $R$ if and only if inertia acts trivially on $T_\ell(A_K)$, equivalently on $A_K[\ell^\nu](K^{\mathrm{sep}})$ for every $\nu\ge1$.

references.title: S. Bosch, W. Lutkebohmert, M. Raynaud, Neron Models (1990), Chapter 1 (good reduction) and 7.4/5 (Neron-Ogg-Shafarevich)
A. Grothendieck, EGA III (cohomology and base change)
