items.title: An elliptic curve with good reduction and an elliptic curve with bad reduction
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and Dependent Choice as inherited from the supplied local items. (a) [good] Let $E_0$ be the complex elliptic curve of [[ex-elliptic-curve-as-nonaffine-algebraic-group]] (a smooth projective cubic over $\mathbf C$ with the chord-tangent group law), let $R=\mathbf C[[t]]$, $K=\mathbf C((t))$, and let $A=E_0\times_{\mathbf C}R$ be the constant base change. Then $A\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is an abelian scheme of relative dimension $1$ with generic fibre $E_0\otimes_{\mathbf C}K$; by [[thm-abelian-scheme-is-the-neron-model-of-its-generic-fibre]] $A$ is the Neron model of its generic fibre, so the generic fibre has good reduction over $R$ and its special fibre is $E_0$. (b) [bad] Let $k$ be a field of characteristic not $2$ or $3$ with $k$ algebraically closed, let $R=k[[t]]$, $K=k((t))$, and let $E_t$ be the smooth cubic $Y^2Z=X^3+tZ^3$ with $O=[0:1:0]$, an elliptic curve over $K$ by [[thm-plane-cubic-chord-tangent-group-law]]. Then $E_t$ has bad reduction over $R$: there is no abelian scheme $A\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ with generic fibre $E_t$. Indeed, if such $A$ existed, then multiplication by $2$ would be finite etale of rank $4$ by [[lem-multiplication-by-n-on-abelian-scheme]], so $A[2]$ would be finite etale over $R$; by [[lem-finite-etale-lifting-over-complete-dvr]] reduction $A[2](R)\to A[2](k)$ would be bijective with $A[2](k)=\mathbf Z/2\times\mathbf Z/2$ (the special fibre is an elliptic curve in characteristic not $2$), hence $A[2](K)=E_t[2](K)$ would have $4$ elements. But the two-torsion of $E_t$ is computed by [[lem-two-torsion-and-uniqueness-of-plane-cubic-group-law]] as $\{O\}$ together with the roots in $K$ of $x^3+t=0$, and $x^3+t$ is Eisenstein at $t$, so it has no root in $K=k((t))$; thus $E_t[2](K)=\{O\}$, a contradiction. (c) The contrast in (b) is sharp: over the totally ramified extension $k((s))$ with $s^6=t$ the substitution $x=s^2x'$, $y=s^3y'$ identifies $E_t\otimes_k((t))\,k((s))$ with $Y^2Z=X^3+Z^3$, the base change from $k$ of an elliptic curve with good reduction, so $E_t$ has bad reduction over $k[[t]]$ but acquires good reduction after a finite ramified extension. In the contradiction step use properness to extend each K-point of the finite group scheme A[2] uniquely to R, and use 3v(x)=1 to exclude roots. No claim that bad reduction of this singular chosen equation alone excludes a different smooth model is made.

references.title: J. S. Milne, Elliptic Curves, v2.0, Chapter VII (good and bad reduction)
D. Lombardo, Abelian varieties lecture notes (2018), Chapter 1 sections 1-7 (examples of reduction)

items.title: Not every abelian variety over a Dedekind function field extends to an abelian scheme
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and Dependent Choice as inherited. There exist a Dedekind scheme $S$, a function field $K$ and an abelian variety $A_K$ over $K$ such that $A_K$ admits no abelian scheme model, i.e. no good reduction, over $S$. Explicitly, for $k$ algebraically closed of characteristic not $2$ or $3$, $R=k[[t]]$, $K=k((t))$, the elliptic curve $E_t:Y^2Z=X^3+tZ^3$ over $K$ with origin $O=[0:1:0]$ has no abelian scheme model over $R$: if $A\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ were one, then the finite etale group scheme $A[2]$ of rank $4$ would satisfy $A[2](K)\to A[2](k)$ bijective with target of order $4$, whereas the two-torsion of $A_K=E_t$ is the set $\{O\}\cup\{\text{roots of }x^3+t\}$, which is a single point because $x^3+t$ is Eisenstein over $k[[t]]$. This contradiction proves the asserted absence of an abelian scheme model. For the hypothetical model, properness identifies A[2](K) with A[2](R), while finite etale lifting identifies the latter with A[2](k). The special fibre has dimension one and its two-torsion has four geometric points by the multiplication theorem. The valuation equality 3v(x)=v(t)=1 proves directly that x^3+t has no root in k((t)); Eisenstein is an alternative, not a needed supplier. The example's explicit ramified extension shows that good reduction need not descend through that ramified extension.

references.title: J. S. Milne, Elliptic Curves, v2.0, Chapter VII (bad reduction examples)
D. Lombardo, Abelian varieties lecture notes (2018), Chapter 1 sections 1-7 (absence of good models)
